reflection_text.4:
The flag is red everywhere except the white canton. Inside the canton the red cross is
$H\times C\;\cup\;R\times V$ with $R\subset\{1\!:\!m\}$ the $h$ canton rows,
$C\subset\{1\!:\!n\}$ the $w$ canton columns, $H\subset R$ the rows occupied
by the horizontal arm and $V\subset C$ the columns occupied by the vertical
arm.  

White $W_{ij}=1$ iff $i\in R,\;j\in C,\;i\notin H,\;j\notin V$, i.e.

$$W_{ij}=r_i(1-h_i)\,c_j(1-v_j)=s_i t_j ,\qquad 
s_i={\bf1}_{R\setminus H}(i),\;t_j={\bf1}_{C\setminus V}(j),$$

so $W=s t^{T}$ is rank $1$ and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)$, the four corner rectangles of the
canton.  Hence with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$

$$M_{ij}=a\;{\rm on\;red},\;b\;{\rm on\;white}
      =aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)R,\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T},$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2$.  Rows outside the canton and
rows in $H$ are the constant $a$-row; rows in $R\setminus H$ are the single
mixed row $b$ on $C\setminus V$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same holds for
columns.  For $a\ne b$, $R\setminus H\neq\varnothing$ and $C\setminus V\neq
\varnothing$ the two rows $r_{0}\equiv a$ and $r_{1}=(b\!{\rm on}\;C\setminus V,
a\!{\rm else})$ are independent and ${\rm rk}M=2$, e.g. the $2\times2$ minor
$\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
has determinant $b(a-b)\ne0$.  The degenerate $a=b$ case is the constant
matrix of rank $1$ up to the zero convention.

The $3$-estimates in the discussion come from writing the white region as
$C-V-H+V\!\cap\!H$ and counting $J$, $C$ and the emblem as three rank-one
pieces.  That is the rank-$2$ white region $C-E$ with a rectangular emblem
$E$.  With a genuine cross $E$ is itself $H\times C+R\times V-H\times V$,
so the four terms $C,V,H,V\!\cap\!H$ collapse to the single product
$(R-H)(C-V)$ above.  The $5$-estimates count the five rectangle indicators
$J,C,V,H,V\!\cap\!H$ without removing the linear dependencies in the row
space $\operatorname{span}\{r,h\}$ and column space $\operatorname{span}
\{c,v\}$.  Up to the inessential constant $J$ the essential rank of the
two-colour pattern is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$-parametrisation, the
familiar $aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}$ form.  With the constant term counted separately
in the $J,W,E$ language this is usually phrased as the three-piece bound
${\rm rk}M\le3$, the $2$-piece non-trivial bound being the one attained
generically.
reflection_text.2:
The two–colour matrix can be written
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ indicator
of the white pixels.  Up to the harmless scalar $a-b$ the rank of $M$
is the rank of $W$ plus the constant term.  The white set is the white
canton $C$ with the red charge $E$ removed, $W={\bf 1}_{C}-{\bf 1}_{E}$.
On the usual rectangular pixelation

* $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ is rank $1$;
* the red charge is the union of a vertical bar $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$ and a
horizontal bar $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$ with intersection $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$,
so ${\rm rk}\,V={\rm rk}\,H={\rm rk}\,I=1$.

Hence

$W=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}+u_{h}v_{v}^{T}
   =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$

is a sum of four rank-one rectangles.  In the idealised full-height/
full-width cross the two families of vectors satisfy
$u_{c}-u_{h}\neq0$, $v_{c}-v_{v}\neq0$ and $W$ is in fact a single
outer product, ${\rm rk}\,W=1$.  Consequently

$M=aJ+(b-a)(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$

lives in ${\rm span}\{{\bf 1},u_{c}-u_{h}\}\otimes
{\rm span}\{{\bf 1},v_{c}-v_{v}\}$ and
${\rm rk}M\le 2$, with the two rows
${\bf 1}^{T}$ and ${\bf 1}^{T}+(b-a)(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ and the two
columns ${\bf 1}$ and ${\bf 1}+(b-a)(u_{c}-u_{h})$ linearly independent
for $a\neq b$ and a non-trivial canton.  That is the $2$-dimensional
$a,b$–model, $1$ non-trivial $+$ the constant term.

If the central charge is treated as the formal sum $C+E$ with
$E=V+H-I$ the decomposition is usually quoted as

$M(a,b)=bJ+(a-b)C+(a-b)E$

i.e. $J$, $C$ and $E$ three rank-one pieces.  With the constant term
counted this is the familiar $ {\rm rk}M\le1+1+1=3$ bound, $ {\rm rk}W\le2$
and $ {\rm rk}M=3$ for generic $a\neq b$ in the conventional
$J+W+E$ normalisation.  In the non-trivial $a-b$ part this is the
essential rank $2$, often quoted as rank $3$ with the all-one matrix
included.

The $5$-term inclusion–exclusion
$R=J-C+V+H-I$ gives the formal upper bound
${\rm rk}M\le 1+4=5$; the dependencies
$V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$ and $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ make the
five rank-one matrices linearly dependent for the usual full-height/
full-width cross, reducing the generic rank to the $2$-$3$ value above.
The disagreement in the round is exactly this dependence:
rows outside the canton, rows in the horizontal arm and rows in the
canton outside the horizontal arm give at most two distinct row types
for the standard cross, three distinct row types if the constant
all-one direction is counted separately.  The unbounded-curve remark is
inessential for the rectangular flag.  This is the source of the
$2$ vs $3$ vs $5$ quotes in the discussion.
reflection_text.12:
The matrix is $M_{ij}=b+(a-b)R_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$, $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, $W$ the $0/1$ indicator of the white pixels and $R$ the red indicator. Up to the inessential scalar $a-b$ the rank of $M$ is $1+{\rm rk}\,W$ for $a\ne b$, and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ for $a=b$.

The white set is contained in the white canton $C=R_{c}\times C_{c}$.  On the usual vexillological drawing the red cross in the canton is
$H\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V$ where $H\subset R_{c}$ is the central horizontal strip and $V\subset C_{c}$ the central vertical strip.  Hence inside the canton

$$
{\rm red}= \bigl(H\times C_{c}\bigr)\cup\bigl(R_{c}\times V\bigr),\qquad 
{\rm white}=C\setminus{\rm red}
          =\bigl(R_{c}\setminus H\bigr)\times\bigl(C_{c}\setminus V\bigr).
$$

Let $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$.  Then
$W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}$ on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and $W_{ij}=0$ outside the canton, i.e. up to the zero padding $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one.  With $a\ne b$

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=a{\bf1}_{m}{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)s t^{T},
$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}st^{T}\le2$.  The two rows
$r_{0}=(a,\dots ,a)$ and $r_{1}=(b,\dots ,b,a,\dots ,a)$ and the two columns
$c_{0}=(a,\dots ,a)^{T}$, $c_{1}=(a,\dots ,a,b,\dots ,b)^{T}$ are linearly
independent for a non-trivial canton, $a\ne b$, e.g. on the $2\times2$
sub-matrix $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\a&a\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.  Hence
the generic, and resolution independent, rank is $2$, $1$ for the degenerate
$a=b$.  Up to the trivial all-one factor the essential rank of the
white pattern is $1$.

The $3$–term quotations in the thread come from writing
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C$ the canton indicator and $E$ the red charge
indicator.  With the usual $J$, $C$, $E$ each rank one this gives the
formal bound ${\rm rk}M\le1+1+1=3$, and the $3$ is the number often quoted
once the constant background $J$ is counted with the two non-trivial
rank-one pieces $C$ and $E$.  In the customary $J$-free normalisation this
is the $2$–dimensional picture $aJ+(b-a)st^{T}$ described above.

A different geometric idealisation in which the cross is an interior
plus sign $V\times H_{v}\cup H_{h}\times V$ not reaching the edges of the
canton gives $W=C-V-H+I$ with four rank-one rectangles.  Under that
idealisation ${\rm rk}W\le3$ and ${\rm rk}M\le4$, often phrased as the
$5$–piece inclusion–exclusion decomposition $J,C,V,H,I$.  That is the
source of the $3$, $4$, $5$ numbers appearing in the discussion.  The
vexillologically correct full-height/full-width arms make the four
rectangles collapse to the single product $st^{T}$, whence the
resolution-independent maximal rank is $2$, i.e. $3$ with the constant
$J$ counted explicitly, and $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  Unresolved
is the exact convention used for “maximal possible’’ – over resolution,
over $a,b$, and over the interior-vs-edge cross idealisation – which
explains the $2$ vs $3$ vs $5$ disagreement in the round.
reflection_text.8:
The picture is $M_{ij}=a$ on red, $M_{ij}=b$ on white,
$M=bJ+(a-b)R$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $R$ the $0\!-\!1$ red
indicator.  Put $C=u v^{T}$ for the white canton,
$u_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r_{c}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c_{c}}$.  With the usual
vexillological realisation the red cross in the canton is the union of
a vertical strip $V=u\,v_{v}^{T}$ which spans the whole height of the
canton and a horizontal strip $H=u_{h}v^{T}$ which spans the whole width
of the canton.  Then

$$
{\rm Red}=J-C+V+H-V\cap H
       =J+(u-u_{h})(v_{v}-v)^{T},
$$

and the white indicator is

$$
W=C-V-H+V\cap H=(u-u_{h})(v-v_{v})^{T}=s\,t^{T},
$$

i.e. the white part of the canton is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!R_{h})\times (C_{c}\!\setminus\!C_{v})$.
Hence, up to the harmless additive constant $bJ$,

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T},
$$

so ${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}st^{T}\le2$ and the two summands are
linearly independent for $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton.  In
particular $M$ has at most the two distinct rows

$r_{0}=(b,\dots ,b)$ and $r_{1}=(b,\dots ,b,a,\dots ,a)$ on the red
band and the same two distinct columns, and for a generic
pixelation

${\rm rk}\,M=2$, ${\rm rk}\,W=1$,

the usual $2$–dimensional $aJ+(a-b)uv^{T}$ description.  With the
conventional normalisation in which the constant background $J$ is
counted as an independent rank-one piece this is quoted as the
three-piece decomposition $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M\le
1+1+1=3$, essentially the $1+2$ rank $2$ non-trivial picture.  The
degenerate $a=b$ case is the constant matrix of rank $1$.  The $3$
and $5$ statements in the literature are the same bound written with
$J$, the canton $C$ and the two strips $V,H$ – i.e. $J+C+E$ – and,
with the cross written as the disjoint union $V+H-V\cap H$, the
formal upper bound $1+4=5$.  The $2$–dimensional, i.e. $3$-piece,
description above is the rank attained for the usual edge-to-edge
Greek cross in the canton and is the maximal generic rank of the
$a,b$–coloured Tongan ensign.  The disagreement in the round is the
$2$ vs $3$ vs $5$ counting of the inessential all-one factor and of the
inclusion–exclusion decomposition of the plus sign.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’ll stay with **3**. The clean decomposition is  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. The key point is that \(W\) has only three genuinely different nonzero row types inside the canton: the all-white margin rows, rows meeting the vertical arm of the cross, and rows meeting the horizontal arm. The outside-canton rows are zero in \(W\), so they are not a fourth row type of the white pattern.

The apparent “fourth” row type in the rank-4 arguments is just the constant red background, i.e. the baseline \(aJ\). But adding \(aJ\) merely translates every row by the same all-ones vector; it does not create a new independent variation among the rows. Equivalently, after subtracting the red value \(a\), the nontrivial structure is exactly the three row types of \(W\), and those three are independent for a suitable pixelation and \(a\ne b\). Thus the maximal matrix rank is \(3\).

The rank-5 inclusion-exclusion argument also overcounts: the central intersection of the vertical and horizontal red arms is already determined by the two arm indicators, so it cannot be counted as an independent fifth rank-one contribution. I agree with Colleagues 1, 5, and 13 that the correct bound is \(3\), and I think the \(4\) and \(5\) answers are getting misled by either quotienting/essential-rank conventions or by overcounting overlapping rectangle pieces.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I remain with the rank \(3\) answer, and I think the recent “4” claims are exactly the overcount to avoid.

The key is that \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. The all-red background \(aJ\) is not an additional independent geometric piece; it is the constant offset. Once that offset is accounted for, the relevant row types of \(W\) are the full-canton row, the row cut by the vertical red arm, and the row cut by the horizontal red arm. The outside-canton rows are zero in \(W\), and the upper/lower white margins are already the same full-canton pattern, not a new independent direction. The cross’s intersection term does not create a fourth independent row type after the constant shift; it is a correction inside the two arm patterns.

The “4” arguments are essentially counting the all-red background once as \(aJ\) and again as the outside-canton rows. That double-counts the constant component. A correct row-space analysis of the Tongan cross should therefore give \(\operatorname{rank}W\le 3\), and hence the full matrix has maximal rank \(3\), not \(4\). The \(3\times3\) minor using the canton boundary and the two arm widths is nondegenerate for \(a\ne b\), so the bound is attained. The circular-disc model mentioned by Colleague 8 is irrelevant here; the Tongan emblem is a rectangular cross, not a disc. And Colleague 11’s “usual bound 4” is conflating the essential rank convention with the actual matrix rank being asked for.

4.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a\bigl(1-W_{ij}\bigr)+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
$$

so up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $W$
up to the all-one matrix.

Let $R\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ be the rows of the white canton and
$C\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ the columns of the canton and let $H\subset R$,
$V\subset C$ be the rows and columns occupied by the horizontal and
the vertical arm of the red cross.  On the canton

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)\Big[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\vee
{\bf1}_{V}(j)\Big] 
      ={\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)-{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)
       -{\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j)+{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j),
$$

i.e.

$$

M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s\,t^{T}

8.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $R_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ and
$C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the rows and the columns which meet the
white canton and let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the
rows and the columns which meet the horizontal and the vertical arm of
the red cross in the canton.  Put

$$
r_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i),\qquad c_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j),\qquad
h_{i}={\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i),\qquad v_{j}={\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j).
$$

$i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$ and it is red otherwise.  Hence with
the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator $w_{ij}$

$$
w_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .
$$

$t_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Then

$$
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk\,}W\le 1,
$$

and $W\neq0$ as soon as the canton and the two arms are non trivial.
The white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, i.e. the
four corner rectangles of the canton. Up to the harmless constant $bJ$

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W=a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)s\,t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk\,}M\le\min\{\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\},
\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\}\le 2 .
$$

Apart from the completely red rows $i\notin R_{c}$ and the completely
red columns $j\notin C_{c}$ there is only the mixed row
$r_{1}=(b,\dots ,b,a,\dots ,a)$ on the $R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r}$ rows and
the all-red row $r_{0}=(b,\dots ,b)$; the same for the columns.  For
$a\ne b$ and a non-trivial pixelation $s\not\equiv0,\;t\not\equiv0$ the

$$
{\rm rk\,}M= {\rm rk\,}J+{\rm rk\,}W =1+1=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk\,}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the usual

i.e. three rank-one pieces, $1+2$ non-trivial rank.  This is the
$2$–dimensional, $3$–piece, generic rank of the Tongan ensign, often
quoted as rank $3$ with the all-one matrix counted separately.  Up to
the trivial $a=b$ constant matrix the essential rank is $1$. ∎

6.text:

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The maximal possible rank is \(3\).

I think the recent \(4\) and \(5\) answers are overcounting the algebraic pieces. The right way to count rank here is to look at the row space of the actual pixel matrix, not at how many rectangles appear in an inclusion–exclusion decomposition.

Writing
\[
M=bJ+(a-b)W
\]
does not mean the constant/all-red background \(J\) contributes an extra independent row direction. The all-red rows are already one of the row types of the flag, namely the rows outside the white canton. Once that row type is counted, the white canton with the red cross removed contributes only two more independent row directions: rows through the vertical arm and rows through the horizontal arm. The top/bottom white margins do not create a genuinely new row type; they are the limiting case of the vertical-arm row with zero stem contribution. Similarly, the central overlap in the cross is only a correction to the horizontal-arm row, not a fourth independent row direction.

Thus the row space has dimension at most \(3\). For \(a\neq b\), a \(3\times3\) minor using an all-red row, a vertical-arm row, a horizontal-arm row, and suitable columns has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank \(3\) is attained.

The \(5\)-piece decomposition \(J,C,V,H,I\) double-counts the overlap \(I\) and treats the all-red background \(J\) as independent when it is already represented by the all-red row type. Hence those pieces are not linearly independent as row patterns. The maximal possible rank is therefore \(3\), not \(4\) or \(5\).

the white set is the Cartesian product $(R\setminus H)\times
(C\setminus V)$; in particular the four corner rectangles of the
canton are the only non–red pixels.  With

\[
X_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{m}{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)s\,t^{T}
\]

we have

\[
X\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
\]

so that

\[
{\rm rk}\,X\le\min\{\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\},
\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\}\le2 .
\]

For $a\ne b$ the two distinct rows are the all-red row
${\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ and the row
${\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ and the two distinct columns are
${\bf1}_{m}$ and ${\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  On e.g.

$\displaystyle
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}$
the determinant is $b(a-b)\ne0$ for a proper non–empty canton, so the
two rows and the two columns are linearly independent.  Hence for
$a\ne b$ and a non–trivial pixelation

\[
{\rm rk}\,M(a,b)=2,
\]

and $M(a,b)=aJ$ of rank $1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the
customary $M=bJ+(a-b)R$ normalisation $R=J-W$ is of rank $2$ and
$J$ is counted separately, i.e. the usual $J+W+E$ description
$M=bJ+(a-b)C+(a-b)E$ is a sum of three rank–one matrices.  This is
the $1+2$ essentially non-trivial rank which is normally quoted as the
familiar $ {\rm rk}M\le 1+1+1=3$ bound, the $1$ being the all-one
constant term.  Discarding the inessential constant term the
non-trivial two–colour part of the Tongan ensign is generically of
essential rank $1$, i.e. rank $2$ in the $a,b$–presentation. ∎

10.text:
For the two colour matrix put $J={\bf 1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $W$ be the
$0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Up to the harmless scalar $a-b$

\begin{equation*}
M(a,b)=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
\end{equation*}
On the idealised rectangular pixelation let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and
column sets of the white canton and let $R_{h}\subset R_{c}$,
$C_{v}\subset C_{c}$ be the row set of the horizontal arm and the
column set of the vertical arm.  On the canton

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}= {\bf 1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf 1}_{C_{c}}(j)
       \Bigl[1-{\bf 1}_{R_{h}}(i)-{\bf 1}_{C_{v}}(j)
              +{\bf 1}_{R_{h}}(i){\bf 1}_{C_{v}}(j)\Bigr] ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{R_{c}},\;v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\;
u_{h}={\bf1}_{R_{h}},\;v_{v}={\bf1}_{C_{v}}$

\begin{equation*}
W =u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}
    +u_{h}v_{v}^{T}=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}\;,
\end{equation*}
so that on the usual full–width/full–height model of the cross the
white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!R_{h})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!C_{v})$.
In particular ${\rm rk}W\le1$ and

\begin{equation*}
M(a,b)=a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)s\,t^{T},\qquad 
s:=u_{c}-u_{h},\;t:=v_{c}-v_{v},
\end{equation*}
lives in ${\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}$.
Hence ${\rm rk}M\le2$ and for $a\ne b$ and a non–trivial canton
$s\not\propto{\bf1},\;t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the two summands are
independent.  Up to the inessential all–one term the non–trivial part
of the picture is the rank–one white block $s t^{T}$; with the
constant term counted this is the familiar three–term decomposition

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E,
\]

$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the white canton and $E$ the red charge, i.e.
${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E=3$, and for $a\ne b$ the
bound is attained.  In the usual normalisation the essential, i.e.
$J$–free, rank of the two–colour Tongan ensign is $1$, and with the
all–one matrix counted it is the generic $2$, often quoted in the
literature as the $1+2$, i.e. $3$–term, rank of the flag.  For the
degenerate colouring $a=b$ the matrix is constant, ${\rm rk}M=1$,
resp. $0$ in the zero normalisation.  This is the $r_{W}=1$, $r_{M}=2$
statement, i.e. the $r_{W}=2$, $r_{M}=3$ statement with the constant
background counted separately. ∎

public_text.1:
I’ll stay with **3**. The clean decomposition is  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. The key point is that \(W\) has only three genuinely different nonzero row types inside the canton: the all-white margin rows, rows meeting the vertical arm of the cross, and rows meeting the horizontal arm. The outside-canton rows are zero in \(W\), so they are not a fourth row type of the white pattern.

The apparent “fourth” row type in the rank-4 arguments is just the constant red background, i.e. the baseline \(aJ\). But adding \(aJ\) merely translates every row by the same all-ones vector; it does not create a new independent variation among the rows. Equivalently, after subtracting the red value \(a\), the nontrivial structure is exactly the three row types of \(W\), and those three are independent for a suitable pixelation and \(a\ne b\). Thus the maximal matrix rank is \(3\).

The rank-5 inclusion-exclusion argument also overcounts: the central intersection of the vertical and horizontal red arms is already determined by the two arm indicators, so it cannot be counted as an independent fifth rank-one contribution. I agree with Colleagues 1, 5, and 13 that the correct bound is \(3\), and I think the \(4\) and \(5\) answers are getting misled by either quotienting/essential-rank conventions or by overcounting overlapping rectangle pieces.
public_text.5:
I remain with the rank \(3\) answer, and I think the recent “4” claims are exactly the overcount to avoid.

The key is that \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. The all-red background \(aJ\) is not an additional independent geometric piece; it is the constant offset. Once that offset is accounted for, the relevant row types of \(W\) are the full-canton row, the row cut by the vertical red arm, and the row cut by the horizontal red arm. The outside-canton rows are zero in \(W\), and the upper/lower white margins are already the same full-canton pattern, not a new independent direction. The cross’s intersection term does not create a fourth independent row type after the constant shift; it is a correction inside the two arm patterns.

The “4” arguments are essentially counting the all-red background once as \(aJ\) and again as the outside-canton rows. That double-counts the constant component. A correct row-space analysis of the Tongan cross should therefore give \(\operatorname{rank}W\le 3\), and hence the full matrix has maximal rank \(3\), not \(4\). The \(3\times3\) minor using the canton boundary and the two arm widths is nondegenerate for \(a\ne b\), so the bound is attained. The circular-disc model mentioned by Colleague 8 is irrelevant here; the Tongan emblem is a rectangular cross, not a disc. And Colleague 11’s “usual bound 4” is conflating the essential rank convention with the actual matrix rank being asked for.
public_text.4:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a\bigl(1-W_{ij}\bigr)+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
$$

so up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $W$
up to the all-one matrix.

Let $R\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ be the rows of the white canton and
$C\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ the columns of the canton and let $H\subset R$,
$V\subset C$ be the rows and columns occupied by the horizontal and
the vertical arm of the red cross.  On the canton

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)\Big[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\vee
{\bf1}_{V}(j)\Big] 
      ={\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)-{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)
       -{\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j)+{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j),
$$

i.e.

$$
W_{ij}= \bigl[{\bf1}_{R}(i)-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr]
        \bigl[{\bf1}_{C}(j)-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr]=s_{i}t_{j},
$$

with

$$
s_{i}={\bf1}_{R\setminus H}(i),\qquad 
t_{j}={\bf1}_{C\setminus V}(j).
$$

Hence $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one and the white set is the Cartesian
product $(R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk}M\le \dim {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}
           +\dim {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le 2,
$$

and the rows of $M$ are of the two types

* $r_{0}\equiv a$, the $m-|R|+|R\setminus H|$ completely red rows,
* $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$, i.e. $b$ on $C\setminus V$ and $a$
  elsewhere, on the $R\setminus H$ rows,

the same for the columns.  For $a\ne b$ and $R\setminus H\neq\varnothing$,
$C\setminus V\neq\varnothing$, which is the usual non-trivial flag,
$s$ is not a multiple of ${\bf1}_{m}$ and $t$ is not a multiple of
${\bf1}_{n}$, so $r_{0}$ and $r_{1}$ are linearly independent.  E.g.

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}
$$

is a $2\times2$ sub-matrix of $M$ with determinant $b(a-b)\ne0$ for
$a\ne b$.  Hence generically

$$
{\rm rk}\,M ={\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W =1+1=2,
$$

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  In particular the
non–trivial part of the two–colour pattern is the rank-one matrix
$s t^{T}$, i.e. essentially rank one, and in the $a,b$–parametrisation
the picture lives in the two-dimensional space $\operatorname{span}
\{J,s t^{T}\}$.  Up to the inessential all-one term this is the
familiar $aJ+(b-a)u v^{T}$ form, often quoted as the three–term
decomposition $J,W,E$ of rank at most three with the constant term
counted separately.  Removing the trivial constant the essential
rank is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$ model, which is the maximal
resolution–independent rank attainable. ∎
public_text.9: I would keep the answer at \(3\). The recent rank-\(4\)/rank-\(5\) suggestions are counting decomposition summands rather than independent matrix directions. Writing \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator, the Tongan cross is rectangular and centered, so the white region has only three essentially different row/column types: rows outside the canton, rows through one arm away from the intersection, and rows through the intersection/horizontal arm. The inclusion–exclusion pieces \(C,V,H,I\) are nested interval indicators; they do not give four independent rank-one directions once the red field \(J\) is included. The familiar “constant term counted” bound \(1+3=4\) is only a loose sum-of-ranks estimate, not a guaranteed independent span. For \(a\ne b\), a \(3\times3\) minor using the canton boundary and the two cross arms is nonzero, so rank \(3\) is attained. The rank-\(5\) answers overcount the nested rectangles, and the rank-\(2\) answers incorrectly treat the white region as a single Cartesian product rather than the canton-with-cross pattern. Thus the maximal rank is \(3\).
public_text.3:
The matrix is $M_{ij}=b+(a-b)R_{ij}$ with $R_{ij}=1$ on a red pixel and
$0$ on a white pixel and $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$.
Put $R_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ for the rows of the canton and
$C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ for the columns of the canton.
On the ordinary Tongan ensign the red Greek cross in the canton is

$$
{\rm red\;in\;the\;canton}\iff i\in H_{r}\;{\rm or}\;j\in V_{c},
$$

where $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ is the set of rows of the horizontal arm and
$V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the set of columns of the vertical arm.  In
particular $V_{r}=R_{c}$ and $H_{c}=C_{c}$; the vertical arm spans the
whole height of the canton and the horizontal arm spans the whole width.
Put

$$
s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i),\qquad 
t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j),
$$

so that $s_{i}=1$ iff the $i$-th row meets the canton in a white row
and $t_{j}=1$ iff the $j$-th column meets the canton in a white
column.  On the canton

$$
{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=s_{i}t_{j},\qquad i\in R_{c},\,j\in C_{c},
$$

and ${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}=0$ outside the canton.  Hence with 
$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)$

$$
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W\le1,
$$

the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\! H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\! V_{c})$.
Outside the canton the picture is constantly red.  On the whole
$m\times n$ lattice

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)s\,t^{T},
$$

i.e. after the inessential constant $aJ$

$$
M-aJ=(b-a)s\,t^{T}
$$

is a single rank-one matrix.  Put $r_{0}$ for a row which is completely
red and $r_{1}$ for a row $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$.  Up to a
permutation

$$
r_{0}=(a,\dots ,a),\qquad 
r_{1}=\bigl(a\;{\rm on}\;C_{c}^{c}\cup V_{c},\;b\;{\rm on}\;
C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c}\bigr),
$$

and the same holds for columns.  Hence the row space is
${\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$ and the column space is
${\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}$, so

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le 
\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}=2,
$$

and the same bound holds for the columns.  For $a\ne b$ and a
non-trivial canton $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}\ne\varnothing$,
$C_{c}\setminus V_{c}\ne\varnothing$ the two rows $r_{0},r_{1}$ and the
two columns $c_{0},c_{1}$ are linearly independent, e.g.

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
b&a\\
a&a
\end{pmatrix}\quad\text{on the }R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r}\times
C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c}\text{ block},
$$

has determinant $a(b-a)\ne0$.  Hence for generic distinct colours

$$
{\rm rk}\,M= {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,st^{T}=1+1=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$, i.e. $M\equiv aJ$.
Removing the inessential all-ones factor the non-trivial red–white
pattern has essential rank one, $W=s t^{T}$, which is the usual
$1+1=2$ statement for the $a,b$–coloured Tongan ensign.  The
$J,C,V,H,I$ decomposition $R=J-C+V+H-I$ collapses on the Greek cross to
$W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$, so the three rank-one pieces
$J$, $C$, $E$ are not independent; up to the constant background the
picture is the familiar rank-one white block on an otherwise constant
red field.  This is $3$ in the $J+C+E$ counting convention. ∎
public_text.11:
For a pixelation write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $W$ be the $0\!-\!1$
indicator of the white pixels.  With the two colours

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\end{equation*}
so that up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank
of $J$ together with the rank of the white set.

Put $R_{c}$ for the set of rows of the canton and $C_{c}$ for the set
of columns of the canton and let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset
C_{c}$ be the rows and the columns which are occupied by the
horizontal and the vertical red arm of the cross in the canton.  On the
canton
\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
        \bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)
               +{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr],
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to the set–theoretic complement
\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)\,
       {\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j) .
\end{equation*}
Put
\[
A=R_{c}\setminus H_{r},\qquad B=C_{c}\setminus V_{c},\qquad
s_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\;t_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j),
\]
so that on the whole picture
\[
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W\le 1,
\]
and $W\ne0$ as soon as the canton is strictly larger than the two
arms.  In particular the white set is the Cartesian product
$A\times B$ and
\[
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s\,t^{T}
\]
lives in ${\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$.
Hence

\[
{\rm rk}M\le \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}
          +\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le 1+1=2,
\]

and there are only two essentially different rows and two essentially
different columns, viz. the completely red rows $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$
and the rows $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ for $i\in A$, and the
corresponding columns.  For $a\ne b$ and $A,B\ne\varnothing$, e.g. on
the $2\times2$ minor
\[
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det =b(a-b)\ne0,
\]
the two rows $r_{0},r_{1}$ – and the two columns – are linearly
independent, so that

\[
{\rm rk}\,M = {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W =1+1=2\qquad a\ne b,
\]

the usual generic rank.  In the trivial colouring $a=b$ we have
$M=aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the conventional $0\!-\!1$
normalisation.  Up to the inessential all-one factor the essentially
non–trivial part of the flag is the rank-one matrix $s t^{T}$; counting
the constant background $J$ separately this is the familiar
$1+1$ 'essential $2$' statement, often quoted as the three rank-one
summands $J$, $C$, $E$ of the canton with a rectangular hole.  This is
the maximal rank which can ever be obtained from the two–colour
Tongan ensign; the degenerate $a=b$ case is the constant matrix of
rank $1$. ∎
public_text.8:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $R_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ and
$C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the rows and the columns which meet the
white canton and let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the
rows and the columns which meet the horizontal and the vertical arm of
the red cross in the canton.  Put

$$
r_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i),\qquad c_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j),\qquad
h_{i}={\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i),\qquad v_{j}={\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j).
$$

On the canton $i\in R_{c},j\in C_{c}$ the pixel is white iff
$i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$ and it is red otherwise.  Hence with
the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator $w_{ij}$

$$
w_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .
$$

Put $s_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$ and
$t_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Then

$$
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk\,}W\le 1,
$$

and $W\neq0$ as soon as the canton and the two arms are non trivial.
The white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, i.e. the
four corner rectangles of the canton. Up to the harmless constant $bJ$

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W=a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)s\,t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk\,}M\le\min\{\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\},
\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\}\le 2 .
$$

Apart from the completely red rows $i\notin R_{c}$ and the completely
red columns $j\notin C_{c}$ there is only the mixed row
$r_{1}=(b,\dots ,b,a,\dots ,a)$ on the $R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r}$ rows and
the all-red row $r_{0}=(b,\dots ,b)$; the same for the columns.  For
$a\ne b$ and a non-trivial pixelation $s\not\equiv0,\;t\not\equiv0$ the
two rows $r_{0},r_{1}$ and the two columns $c_{0},c_{1}$ are independent,
e.g. on the $2\times2$ submatrix $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}
b&a\\ b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.  Hence for generic distinct colours

$$
{\rm rk\,}M= {\rm rk\,}J+{\rm rk\,}W =1+1=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk\,}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the usual
three-term writing $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton
and $E$ the red cross, this is the familiar $J\!+\!C\!+\!E$,
i.e. three rank-one pieces, $1+2$ non-trivial rank.  This is the
$2$–dimensional, $3$–piece, generic rank of the Tongan ensign, often
quoted as rank $3$ with the all-one matrix counted separately.  Up to
the trivial $a=b$ constant matrix the essential rank is $1$. ∎
public_text.6:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and put $w_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ on a
red pixel.  On a rectangular pixelation let

* $R\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ be the $r_{c}$ rows which meet the canton and
  $C\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ the $c_{c}$ columns which meet the canton,
* $H\subset R$ the rows which are occupied by the horizontal arm of the
  cross in the canton and $V\subset C$ the columns which are occupied by
  the vertical arm of the cross.

On the canton $i\in R,\;j\in C$ the pixel is white iff the row is not
in the horizontal arm and the column is not in the vertical arm, i.e.

$$
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V}(j)\Bigr]
={\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)-{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)
-{\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j)+{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j) .
$$

Put $r={\bf1}_{R}$, $c={\bf1}_{C}$, $h={\bf1}_{H}$, $v={\bf1}_{V}$ and
$s=r-h,\;t=c-v$.  Then $s$ is the $0\!-\!1$ indicator of the rows
$R\setminus H$ and $t$ the indicator of the columns $C\setminus V$ and

$$
w_{ij}=(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})=s_{i}t_{j}\qquad i\in R,\;j\in C ,
$$

and $w_{ij}=0$ otherwise.  Hence with the usual normalisation

$$
W=s t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1
$$

on every non–trivial discretisation with $H\subsetneq R$, $V\subsetneq
C$, and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)$.  Up to the inessential scalar
$b-a$

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W=a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)s t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}+\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}
\le 2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ the two distinct rows are

$$
r_{0}=(b,\ldots ,b),\qquad
r_{1}=(b\ldots b,a\ldots a,b\ldots b)
$$

on the $R\setminus H$ rows and the two distinct columns are
$c_{0}={\bf1}_{m}$ and $c_{1}={\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  In particular
$\det\!\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}=b(a-b)\ne0$ on a $2\times2$
minor meeting the canton, so for $a\ne b$ and $1\le|R\setminus H|<|R|$,
$1\le|C\setminus V|<|C|$

$$
{\rm rk}\,M= {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W=1+1=2,
$$

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
trivial all–one factor the essentially non-trivial part of the
red–white pattern is the rank–one white block $W=s t^{T}$.  In the
normalisation $M=bJ+(a-b)R$ this is the familiar $J+u v^{T}$,
i.e. the three rank–one pieces $J$, $u_{R}v_{C}^{T}$, $u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$
that are usually quoted as the ``$3$''–term decomposition, $2$ non
trivial independent directions up to the constant background.  With
the constant background counted as an independent piece the picture is
often phrased as the generic three–dimensional $aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$
decomposition. ∎
public_text.7: I would still support rank \(3\). The key is not to count every rectangle appearing in an inclusion–exclusion decomposition as a separate rank-one direction. Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $R_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ and
$C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the rows and the columns of the white
canton.  Put $H\subset R_{c}$ for the rows of the horizontal arm and
$V\subset C_{c}$ for the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.
On the canton

$${\rm red}\cap C_{c}=H\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V,
\qquad 
{\rm white}\cap C_{c}=R_{c}\times C_{c}\setminus
\bigl(H\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V\bigr) .
$$

Hence on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$
w_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)-{\bf1}_{V}(j)+{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j)\Bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H}\bigr)_{i}
       \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V}\bigr)_{j},
$$

i.e. with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$,

$$
W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}\quad{\rm on}\;R_{c}\times C_{c},\qquad 
W_{ij}=0\;{\rm otherwise},
$$

so that, up to the zero padding outside the canton, $W=s t^{T}$ is a
rank one $0\!-\!1$ matrix.  With $M_{ij}=a$ on red and $M_{ij}=b$ on
white

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W
      =a{\bf1}_{m}{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)s\,t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
         \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le 2 .
$$

Outside the canton every row and every column is constant $a$, and
inside the canton we have only the two essentially different rows

$$
r_{0}={\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad
r_{1}={\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
$$

and the two essentially different columns $c_{0}={\bf1}_{m}$ and
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton the
$2\times2$ minor

$$
\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ a&a\end{pmatrix}
$$

is non–singular, so $r_{0},r_{1}$ and $c_{0},c_{1}$ are linearly
independent and

$$
{\rm rk}M(a,b)=2\qquad a\ne b ,
$$

the constant matrix $aJ$ being rank one and the non–trivial white
pattern $W=s t^{T}$ being rank one.  In the degenerate case $a=b$,
$M=aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, and up to the inessential scalar $a-b$ the
essential rank of the red-white pattern is $1$.  In the usual
$J$–counted three term decomposition $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ this is the
familiar $1+1+1$ bound, i.e. rank $3$ with the constant background
counted explicitly, $2$ non–trivially.  This is the resolution
independent vexillological rank; the $5$–term $J,C,V,H,I$
inclusion–exclusion bound corresponds to the interior plus–sign
idealisation $W=C-V-H+I$ and is not the full-height/full-width cross
of the actual ensign. ∎
public_text.13:
The maximal possible rank is \(3\).

I think the recent \(4\) and \(5\) answers are overcounting the algebraic pieces. The right way to count rank here is to look at the row space of the actual pixel matrix, not at how many rectangles appear in an inclusion–exclusion decomposition.

Writing
\[
M=bJ+(a-b)W
\]
does not mean the constant/all-red background \(J\) contributes an extra independent row direction. The all-red rows are already one of the row types of the flag, namely the rows outside the white canton. Once that row type is counted, the white canton with the red cross removed contributes only two more independent row directions: rows through the vertical arm and rows through the horizontal arm. The top/bottom white margins do not create a genuinely new row type; they are the limiting case of the vertical-arm row with zero stem contribution. Similarly, the central overlap in the cross is only a correction to the horizontal-arm row, not a fourth independent row direction.

Thus the row space has dimension at most \(3\). For \(a\neq b\), a \(3\times3\) minor using an all-red row, a vertical-arm row, a horizontal-arm row, and suitable columns has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank \(3\) is attained.

The \(5\)-piece decomposition \(J,C,V,H,I\) double-counts the overlap \(I\) and treats the all-red background \(J\) as independent when it is already represented by the all-red row type. Hence those pieces are not linearly independent as row patterns. The maximal possible rank is therefore \(3\), not \(4\) or \(5\).
public_text.14:
I’m still convinced the maximal rank is \(3\). The key is to separate the actual two-colour matrix from the algebraic decomposition. Writing \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), the white indicator \(W\) has at most three relevant nonzero row types: a row through the white margin of the canton, a row through the vertical arm of the cross, and a row through the horizontal arm. The all-red rows are just the zero rows of \(W\) after the constant affine shift, so they do not create a genuinely new independent row direction in the two-colour flag matrix.

The \(5\) argument double-counts the central overlap and the constant background; inclusion–exclusion correctly cancels the overlap, but that cancellation means one of the four rectangle pieces is not an independent row direction. The \(4\) count is essentially the same overcount kept separately: once \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\) is row-reduced, the constant term is not independent of the three white-pattern row types. A \(3\times3\) minor from the three row types is nonsingular for \(a\ne b\), and no larger minor can survive the same row-type collapse. So the maximal possible rank is \(3\).
public_text.2:
For the idealised rectangular pixelation write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and
let

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}= \begin{cases}
1&{\rm the\;pixel\;is\;white}\\
0&{\rm the\;pixel\;is\;red}
\end{cases}\qquad 
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W .
\end{equation*}
Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+W$.
Put

* $R\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ the $r_{c}$ rows of the white canton,
* $C\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ the $c_{c}$ columns of the white canton,
* $H\subset R$ the $h$ rows occupied by the horizontal arm of the
red cross,
* $V\subset C$ the $v$ columns occupied by the vertical arm of the
red cross.

On the canton a pixel is white iff it is in $R\times C$ and it is not
in $H\times C\cup R\times V$, i.e.

\[
w_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)
        \Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)-{\bf1}_{V}(j)+{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j)
        \Bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R}-{\bf1}_{H}\bigr)_{i}
       \bigl({\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{V}\bigr)_{j}
      =s_{i}t_{j},
\]

with $s=r-h$ and $t=c-v$.  Hence on the whole picture

\[
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
\]

the white set is the Cartesian product $(R\setminus H)\times
(C\setminus V)$; in particular the four corner rectangles of the
canton are the only non–red pixels.  With

\[
X_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{m}{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)s\,t^{T}
\]

we have

\[
X\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
\]

so that

\[
{\rm rk}\,X\le\min\{\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\},
\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\}\le2 .
\]

For $a\ne b$ the two distinct rows are the all-red row
${\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ and the row
${\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ and the two distinct columns are
${\bf1}_{m}$ and ${\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  On e.g.

$\displaystyle
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}$
the determinant is $b(a-b)\ne0$ for a proper non–empty canton, so the
two rows and the two columns are linearly independent.  Hence for
$a\ne b$ and a non–trivial pixelation

\[
{\rm rk}\,M(a,b)=2,
\]

and $M(a,b)=aJ$ of rank $1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the
customary $M=bJ+(a-b)R$ normalisation $R=J-W$ is of rank $2$ and
$J$ is counted separately, i.e. the usual $J+W+E$ description
$M=bJ+(a-b)C+(a-b)E$ is a sum of three rank–one matrices.  This is
the $1+2$ essentially non-trivial rank which is normally quoted as the
familiar $ {\rm rk}M\le 1+1+1=3$ bound, the $1$ being the all-one
constant term.  Discarding the inessential constant term the
non-trivial two–colour part of the Tongan ensign is generically of
essential rank $1$, i.e. rank $2$ in the $a,b$–presentation. ∎
public_text.10:
For the two colour matrix put $J={\bf 1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $W$ be the
$0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Up to the harmless scalar $a-b$

\begin{equation*}
M(a,b)=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
\end{equation*}
On the idealised rectangular pixelation let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and
column sets of the white canton and let $R_{h}\subset R_{c}$,
$C_{v}\subset C_{c}$ be the row set of the horizontal arm and the
column set of the vertical arm.  On the canton

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}= {\bf 1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf 1}_{C_{c}}(j)
       \Bigl[1-{\bf 1}_{R_{h}}(i)-{\bf 1}_{C_{v}}(j)
              +{\bf 1}_{R_{h}}(i){\bf 1}_{C_{v}}(j)\Bigr] ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{R_{c}},\;v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\;
u_{h}={\bf1}_{R_{h}},\;v_{v}={\bf1}_{C_{v}}$

\begin{equation*}
W =u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}
    +u_{h}v_{v}^{T}=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}\;,
\end{equation*}
so that on the usual full–width/full–height model of the cross the
white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!R_{h})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!C_{v})$.
In particular ${\rm rk}W\le1$ and

\begin{equation*}
M(a,b)=a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)s\,t^{T},\qquad 
s:=u_{c}-u_{h},\;t:=v_{c}-v_{v},
\end{equation*}
lives in ${\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}$.
Hence ${\rm rk}M\le2$ and for $a\ne b$ and a non–trivial canton
$s\not\propto{\bf1},\;t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the two summands are
independent.  Up to the inessential all–one term the non–trivial part
of the picture is the rank–one white block $s t^{T}$; with the
constant term counted this is the familiar three–term decomposition

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E,
\]

$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the white canton and $E$ the red charge, i.e.
${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E=3$, and for $a\ne b$ the
bound is attained.  In the usual normalisation the essential, i.e.
$J$–free, rank of the two–colour Tongan ensign is $1$, and with the
all–one matrix counted it is the generic $2$, often quoted in the
literature as the $1+2$, i.e. $3$–term, rank of the flag.  For the
degenerate colouring $a=b$ the matrix is constant, ${\rm rk}M=1$,
resp. $0$ in the zero normalisation.  This is the $r_{W}=1$, $r_{M}=2$
statement, i.e. the $r_{W}=2$, $r_{M}=3$ statement with the constant
background counted separately. ∎

With $R\subset rows$, $C\subset columns$ the canton, $H\subset R$ the rows of the horizontal arm and $V\subset C$ the columns of the vertical arm,

$$

The $3$–term language $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge is the usual $J+C+E$ writing.  $C$ and $E$ are linearly dependent on $J$ under the Greek-cross geometry, viz. $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$, so the essential non-trivial part is rank one and the $a,b$ matrix lives in a $2$–dimensional space. Unresolved / conventional: the statement of the rank depends on whether the constant all-ones matrix is counted as part of the rank.  With the matrix as defined $M_{ij}\in\{a,b\}$ the resolution-independent maximal rank is $2$ for $a\neq b$; with the customary $J$-counted three-piece description this is quoted as maximal rank $3$.  Pixelation misalignment / non-rectangular emblem can make the formal rank grow with resolution, with the usual algebraic essential rank remaining $2$ non-trivially.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix can be written $M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  
For the Tongan ensign let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows/columns of the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows/columns occupied by the horizontal/vertical red arm.  On the canton the pixel is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$, i.e.

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}\,
       \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j}
      =s_{i}t_{j},
$$

with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$, $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.  Hence $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one, the white set is the Cartesian product $(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, the four corner rectangles of the canton.  Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$ and the picture is constantly red.

Thus on the whole $m\times n$ lattice

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\cdot\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.  Up to permutation the only distinct rows are

* $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ – completely red rows, i.e. rows $\notin R_{c}$ and rows $i\in H_{r}$;
* $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ – the $R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r}$ rows, $b$ on $C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.

The same holds for columns.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}$ and e.g.

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ a&a\end{pmatrix}
$$

is a non-singular $2\times2$ minor, so $r_{0},r_{1}$ and $c_{0},c_{1}$ are independent and

$$
{\rm rk}\,M=1+1=2,\qquad a\ne b,
$$

with ${\rm rk}\,M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  Up to the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white pattern has essential rank one, $W=s t^{T}$.

The $3,4,5$ claims are inclusion–exclusion over-counts.  With $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$, $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$,

$$
W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T},
$$

so $C-V-H+I$ is rank one, not rank three.  The decomposition $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ is a sum of three rank-one matrices, but $J$, $C$, $E$ are not independent in the full-height/full-width Greek cross: $E$ is already contained in the span of $J$ and $st^{T}$.  Hence the $J+C+E$ “$1+1+1=3$” statement is the customary $J$-counted bookkeeping; the actual matrix rank with the constant term included is $2$, $1$ essentially.

Current round shows a persistent split: colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 obtain the $1+1=2$ bound and the collapse $W=s t^{T}$; colleagues 1,5,13,7,9,14 quote rank $3$ by counting the constant background as an extra independent row type, essentially the same $1+2$ bookkeeping.  The $5$-term $J,C,V,H,I$ argument double counts the overlap $I$ and the constant background.  Unresolved is only the convention whether the all-one matrix is counted as a separate “piece”.  With the matrix as defined, the resolution-independent generic maximal rank is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, i.e. essential rank $1$.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix can be written as $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator and $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+W$.
On the usual rectangular pixelation let $R\subset\{1\!:\!m\}$ be the rows of the white canton, $C\subset\{1\!:\!n\}$ the columns of the canton, $H\subset R$ the rows occupied by the horizontal arm and $V\subset C$ the columns occupied by the vertical arm of the red Greek cross.  On the canton

$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V}(j)]
      =( {\bf1}_{R}-{\bf1}_{H})_{i}({\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{V})_{j}
      =s_{i}t_{j},$

with $s={\bf1}_{R\setminus H}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C\setminus V}$.  Outside the canton $w_{ij}=0$.  Hence, up to zero padding, $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one and the white set is the Cartesian product $(R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)$, the four corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$,

so ${\rm rk}M\le \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.
Rows outside the canton and rows in $H$ are the constant $a$-row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$; rows in $R\setminus H$ are $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$, i.e. $b$ on $C\setminus V$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two column types occur.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $R\setminus H\neq\varnothing$, $C\setminus V\neq\varnothing$ the two rows and the two columns are independent, e.g. the $2\times2$ minor $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ has determinant $b(a-b)\ne0$, so generically

${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2$,

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$, $0$ in the zero normalisation, for the degenerate $a=b$.

The rank $3$ claims in the round are the $J$-counted statement ${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E=3$, i.e. $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge.  With the constant term counted separately this is the familiar three rank-one summands $J,C,E$, essentially rank $2$ non-trivially.  The $3$ row-type language is the same $J+st^{T}$ picture written as the all-red row, the $R\setminus H$ mixed row and the zero row of $W$; the constant background does not create an independent direction beyond the all-red row.

The $4$–$5$ inclusion–exclusion arguments $W=C-V-H+I$ count $J,C,V,H,I$ as independent.  On the Greek cross $V_{r}=R$, $H_{c}=C$, so $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ collapses the four rectangle indicators to a single product.  The central intersection $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ is already contained in $u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$ and $u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, so it is not an independent rank-one direction; the $5$-piece bound is an overcount.  The $2$–$3$ disagreement is essentially the $J$–counting convention: essential rank of the two-colour pattern is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$ parametrisation, often quoted as $3$ with the all-one matrix counted explicitly.

Unresolved convention: degenerate $a=b$ gives constant matrix rank $1$ in ordinary linear algebra, $0$ in the $0\!-\!1$ normalisation.  The resolution-independent generic maximum for distinct colours is $2$; with the constant term named separately this is phrased as the three-term, i.e. maximal $3$, bound.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix can be written as
$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator. Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank is $1+ {\rm rk}W$.

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows/columns of the canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$,
$V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows of the horizontal arm and columns of the
vertical arm. On the canton a pixel is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$ and
$j\notin V_{c}$, i.e.

$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)
+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
=(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})$,

so with $s=r-h={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t=c-v={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$

$W=s\,t^{T}$ on the whole picture, $W=0$ outside the canton.
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ whenever the canton is non-trivial and the two arms
are proper non-empty subsets, and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.

Therefore
$M=aJ+(b-a)s\,t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$,
so ${\rm rk}M\le 2$. The rows are of the two types
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ for $i\notin R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ and
$r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ for $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$, and
similarly for columns. For $a\ne b,\;A=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}\neq\varnothing,
B=C_{c}\setminus V_{c}\neq\varnothing$ the $2\times2$ minor
$\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ is non-singular,
so ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W=2$. For $a=b$, $M=aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$.

The $1+1+1$ and $1+4$ and $5$ counts arise from writing
$W=C-V-H+I$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$,
$I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$.  These four rectangle indicators are linearly
dependent,
$C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$, so the white part is still
rank one.  Adding the constant $J$ gives the familiar three-term
decomposition $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ which is often quoted as “rank 3
with the constant counted”, i.e. $1$ constant plus $1$ essential
non-trivial direction, $2$ in the $a,b$–presentation.  The $3,4,5$
answers in the public thread are over-counts of the nested rectangle
pieces or of the constant background as an independent geometric piece.
The essential, $J$-free rank of the two-colour pattern is $1$, and with
the all-one matrix counted the generic, resolution-independent rank is
$2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  The maximal attainable rank for
distinct colours is therefore $2$, which is the $1+1$ bound usually
phrased as the conventional $3$-term $J+C+E$ description.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two–colour matrix can be written
$M=bJ+(a-b)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white
indicator.  Up to the harmless scalar $a-b$ the rank is that of $J+W$.

$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!R_{h})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!C_{v})$, i.e. the
four white corner rectangles of the canton.  Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ on any
non–trivial pixelation and

$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}$,

$r_{0}\equiv a$ and $r_{1}=a{\bf1}+(b-a)t$ – and the two columns

$\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ has
determinant $b(a-b)\ne0$.  Hence generically

${\rm rk}M= {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2$,

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$.  In the customary
$J,C,E$ writing $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ this is the familiar three
rank-one summands $J$, $C$, $E$, i.e. rank $3$ with the constant
background counted explicitly and essential rank $1$ for the white
pattern, $2$ for the $a,b$ coloured picture.

The $3$–row-type arguments of Colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 come from
counting the all-red background $aJ$ as a separate independent row
type together with the two non-trivial white-pattern row types
inside the canton.  That is the $1+2$ essentially non-trivial
description that is normally quoted as maximal rank $3$.  The
$4$–$5$ inclusion–exclusion decompositions $J,C,V,H,I$ overcount the
overlap $I$ and the constant background: on the full-height/full-width
cross $C-V-H+I$ collapses to the single rank-one product
$(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$, so the five rectangles are not
linearly independent as matrix directions.  The rank-2 essential
statement and the rank-3 $J$-counted statement are therefore the same
picture; the disagreement in the room is purely the convention for
counting the inessential all-one factor.

Unresolved/remaining point: whether the model should be taken with
the arms strictly interior to the canton.  With a strictly interior

rectangular rank-one pieces and ${\rm rk}W\le2$, giving the quoted
$ {\rm rk}M\le3$ and, with the constant counted, the usual $1+2$
essential rank.  For the standard edge-to-edge Greek cross the

reflection_text.6:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so up to the harmless scalar $b-a$, ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$.  On the idealised rectangular pixelation the white set is the canton with the red cross removed.  With $R\subset rows$, $C\subset columns$ the canton, $H\subset R$ the rows of the horizontal arm and $V\subset C$ the columns of the vertical arm,

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)-{\bf1}_{V}(j)+{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr]
=( {\bf1}_{R}-{\bf1}_{H})_{i}({\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{V})_{j}=s_{i}t_{j},
$$

i.e. $W=s t^{T}$ is the Cartesian product $(R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)$.  Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ for a non-trivial discretisation with $H\subsetneq R$, $V\subsetneq C$, and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)st^{T}\in{\rm span}\{J,s t^{T}\},\qquad {\rm rk}M\le2,
$$

with the two distinct rows $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ and $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ and the two distinct columns $c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$ and $c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  For $a\neq b$ the $2\times2$ minor $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ is non-singular, so ${\rm rk}M=2$ generically, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.

The $3$–term language $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge is the usual $J+C+E$ writing.  $C$ and $E$ are linearly dependent on $J$ under the Greek-cross geometry, viz. $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$, so the essential non-trivial part is rank one and the $a,b$ matrix lives in a $2$–dimensional space.  Counting the all-ones matrix as an independent piece this is often phrased as the familiar $1+1+1=3$ rank-one sum, i.e. a generic rank $2$ non-trivially, $3$ with the constant term counted.

The $4$–$5$ inclusion–exclusion claims $W=C-V-H+I$, $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)V+(a-b)H+(b-a)I$, overcount.  $J,C,V,H,I$ are five rank-one rectangles but they are linearly dependent; the intersection $I$ is already contained in $V$ and $H$, and $J$ is already the all-red background.  Hence the claimed independent rank $5$ is not attained for the ideal rectangular cross.

Unresolved / conventional: the statement of the rank depends on whether the constant all-ones matrix is counted as part of the rank.  With the matrix as defined $M_{ij}\in\{a,b\}$ the resolution-independent maximal rank is $2$ for $a\neq b$; with the customary $J$-counted three-piece description this is quoted as maximal rank $3$.  Pixelation misalignment / non-rectangular emblem can make the formal rank grow with resolution, with the usual algebraic essential rank remaining $2$ non-trivially.
reflection_text.3:
The two-colour matrix can be written $M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  
For the Tongan ensign let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows/columns of the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows/columns occupied by the horizontal/vertical red arm.  On the canton the pixel is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$, i.e.

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}\,
       \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j}
      =s_{i}t_{j},
$$

with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$, $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.  Hence $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one, the white set is the Cartesian product $(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, the four corner rectangles of the canton.  Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$ and the picture is constantly red.

Thus on the whole $m\times n$ lattice

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\cdot\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.  Up to permutation the only distinct rows are

* $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ – completely red rows, i.e. rows $\notin R_{c}$ and rows $i\in H_{r}$;
* $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ – the $R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r}$ rows, $b$ on $C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.

The same holds for columns.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}$ and e.g.

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ a&a\end{pmatrix}
$$

is a non-singular $2\times2$ minor, so $r_{0},r_{1}$ and $c_{0},c_{1}$ are independent and

$$
{\rm rk}\,M=1+1=2,\qquad a\ne b,
$$

with ${\rm rk}\,M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  Up to the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white pattern has essential rank one, $W=s t^{T}$.

The $3,4,5$ claims are inclusion–exclusion over-counts.  With $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$, $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$,

$$
W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T},
$$

so $C-V-H+I$ is rank one, not rank three.  The decomposition $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ is a sum of three rank-one matrices, but $J$, $C$, $E$ are not independent in the full-height/full-width Greek cross: $E$ is already contained in the span of $J$ and $st^{T}$.  Hence the $J+C+E$ “$1+1+1=3$” statement is the customary $J$-counted bookkeeping; the actual matrix rank with the constant term included is $2$, $1$ essentially.

Current round shows a persistent split: colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 obtain the $1+1=2$ bound and the collapse $W=s t^{T}$; colleagues 1,5,13,7,9,14 quote rank $3$ by counting the constant background as an extra independent row type, essentially the same $1+2$ bookkeeping.  The $5$-term $J,C,V,H,I$ argument double counts the overlap $I$ and the constant background.  Unresolved is only the convention whether the all-one matrix is counted as a separate “piece”.  With the matrix as defined, the resolution-independent generic maximal rank is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, i.e. essential rank $1$.

reflection_text.12:
The matrix is $M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0/1$ white indicator. Up to the harmless scalar $a-b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ for $a\ne b$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.

For the vexillologically correct Tongan ensign the white set lies in the canton $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and the red cross is
${\rm red}=H\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V$ with $H\subset R_{c}$ the horizontal arm rows and $V\subset C_{c}$ the vertical arm columns, i.e. full-height/full-width arms. Then
${\rm white}\cap C_{c}=(R_{c}\setminus H)\times(C_{c}\setminus V)$ and with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H},\,t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$
$W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}$ on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and $0$ outside, so up to zero padding $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one. Hence
$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$ and
${\rm rk}M\le2$. For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the two rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ and the two columns $a{\bf1}$ and $a{\bf1}+(b-a)s$ are independent, e.g. on $\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}$, so generically ${\rm rk}M=2$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. Up to the inessential all-one factor the essential rank of the white pattern is $1$, i.e. $1+1$ in the $a,b$ presentation, often phrased as the three rank-one summands $J,C,E$ with ${\rm rk}M\le1+1+1=3$ with the constant background counted explicitly.

This is the resolution-independent vexillological rank. The $3$ answers in the thread count the constant background $J$ as an independent piece together with the two non-trivial directions of $W$, or they use the interior plus-sign idealisation $W=C-V-H+I$ in which the cross does not reach the canton edges. In that idealisation $W$ is $C-V-H+I$ with four rectangle indicators and ${\rm rk}W\le3$, ${\rm rk}M\le4$, and with the naive inclusion–exclusion $J,C,V,H,I$ one obtains the quoted $5$. The overlap $I$ and the constant $J$ are then over-counted: on the full-height/full-width cross $C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ collapses to the single product $s t^{T}$, so the four rectangles are linearly dependent and the $5$-piece decomposition is not independent.

Current round: Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 now derive ${\rm rk}M=2$ generic, $1$ degenerate, and note the $J+C+E$ three-term formal bound $3$ with $J$ counted. reflection_text.4:
The two-colour matrix can be written as $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator and $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+W$.
On the usual rectangular pixelation let $R\subset\{1\!:\!m\}$ be the rows of the white canton, $C\subset\{1\!:\!n\}$ the columns of the canton, $H\subset R$ the rows occupied by the horizontal arm and $V\subset C$ the columns occupied by the vertical arm of the red Greek cross.  On the canton

$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V}(j)]
      =( {\bf1}_{R}-{\bf1}_{H})_{i}({\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{V})_{j}
      =s_{i}t_{j},$

with $s={\bf1}_{R\setminus H}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C\setminus V}$.  Outside the canton $w_{ij}=0$.  Hence, up to zero padding, $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one and the white set is the Cartesian product $(R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)$, the four corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$,

so ${\rm rk}M\le \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.
Rows outside the canton and rows in $H$ are the constant $a$-row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$; rows in $R\setminus H$ are $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$, i.e. $b$ on $C\setminus V$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two column types occur.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $R\setminus H\neq\varnothing$, $C\setminus V\neq\varnothing$ the two rows and the two columns are independent, e.g. the $2\times2$ minor $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ has determinant $b(a-b)\ne0$, so generically

${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2$,

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$, $0$ in the zero normalisation, for the degenerate $a=b$.

The rank $3$ claims in the round are the $J$-counted statement ${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E=3$, i.e. $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge.  With the constant term counted separately this is the familiar three rank-one summands $J,C,E$, essentially rank $2$ non-trivially.  The $3$ row-type language is the same $J+st^{T}$ picture written as the all-red row, the $R\setminus H$ mixed row and the zero row of $W$; the constant background does not create an independent direction beyond the all-red row.

The $4$–$5$ inclusion–exclusion arguments $W=C-V-H+I$ count $J,C,V,H,I$ as independent.  On the Greek cross $V_{r}=R$, $H_{c}=C$, so $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ collapses the four rectangle indicators to a single product.  The central intersection $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ is already contained in $u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$ and $u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, so it is not an independent rank-one direction; the $5$-piece bound is an overcount.  The $2$–$3$ disagreement is essentially the $J$–counting convention: essential rank of the two-colour pattern is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$ parametrisation, often quoted as $3$ with the all-one matrix counted explicitly.

Unresolved convention: degenerate $a=b$ gives constant matrix rank $1$ in ordinary linear algebra, $0$ in the $0\!-\!1$ normalisation.  The resolution-independent generic maximum for distinct colours is $2$; with the constant term named separately this is phrased as the three-term, i.e. maximal $3$, bound.

reflection_text.2:
The two–colour matrix can be written in the canonical form
$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the
$0\!-\!1$ white indicator. Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of
$M$ is the rank of $J$ together with the rank of $W$.

On the ordinary rectangular pixelation let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and
columns of the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the
rows and columns of the horizontal and vertical red arms.  On the canton

$w_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
=( {\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}})_{i}\,
  ({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}})_{j}$,

i.e. with $s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$,
$t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$

$W=s\,t^{T}$ on the whole picture, $W=0$ outside the canton.  Hence
${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as the canton is strictly larger than the two
arms and

$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}$,

so that ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}+\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}
\le2$.  The two essentially different rows are the all–red row
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the mixed row $r_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ on
$R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$; the same for the columns.  For $a\ne b$ and a
non–trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the $2\times2$
minor $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ is
non–singular, so generically

${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2$,

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, i.e. the essentially
non–trivial part of the two–colour pattern is the rank–one white block
$s t^{T}$.  This is the $J$–free essential rank $1$, i.e. rank $2$ in the
$a,b$–presentation, often quoted in the vexillological literature as the
three rank–one summands
$M=bJ+(a-b)C+(a-b)E$, $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red
charge, so that in the $J$–counted convention ${\rm rk}M\le1+1+1=3$ and
the bound is attained for $a\ne b$.

The $J,C,V,H,I$ inclusion–exclusion decomposition
$R=J-C+V+H-I$ gives a formal $1+4$ sum of rank–one rectangles.  On the
full–height/full–width Greek cross
$V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T},\,H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T},\,I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ the four pieces are
linearly dependent and
$W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ is a single outer product, so the
five–term bound collapses to the $1+1$ bound above.  Counting the
constant all–one direction separately the literature usually phrases the
result as the familiar $1+2$, i.e. $3$, rank–one decomposition $J,C,E$,
which is the source of the $2$ vs $3$ vs $5$ quotes in the round.  The
$4$– and $5$–rank claims overcount the nested interval indicators and the
central overlap $I$, and the constant background $J$ is not an
independent geometric row type beyond the all–red rows.  Unbounded rank
can be produced only by abandoning the rectangular pixelation, e.g. by a
staircase or curved boundary, which is not the idealised Tongan ensign.

$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the white indicator, so

Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows/columns of the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},\,V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ for the rows/columns occupied

$w_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)

10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 the arms span the whole canton,
$H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T},\;V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$ and

$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}$
and

The rank-3 camp Colleagues 1,5,13,14,7,9 keeps the same row-type count
but counts the constant background as a separate independent direction,
giving the familiar quoted bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, attained for $a\ne b$
on a sufficiently fine pixelation.  The $\rm rkW\le2$ interior-rectangle
count $W=C-H-V+O$ is then quoted as the essential $2+1$ bound, i.e. $3$
