4.text:
The two–colour picture is
$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T},
$$
$w_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ on a red pixel.  Up to the harmless
scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+W$.

Let $R\subset\{1\!:\!m\}$ be the rows which meet the white canton,
$C\subset\{1\!:\!n\}$ the columns which meet the canton and let
$H\subset R$, $V\subset C$ be the rows and the columns occupied by the
horizontal and the vertical arm of the red Greek cross in the canton.
On the canton a pixel is white iff the row is not in the horizontal arm
and the column is not in the vertical arm,

$$
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R}(i){\bf1}_{C}(j)\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V}(j)\Bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R}-{\bf1}_{H}\bigr)_{i}
       \bigl({\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{V}\bigr)_{j},\qquad i\in R,\;j\in C,
$$
and $w_{ij}=0$ outside $R\times C$.  Put
$$
s_{i}={\bf1}_{R\setminus H}(i),\qquad 
t_{j}={\bf1}_{C\setminus V}(j).
$$
Then on the whole $m\times n$ lattice, up to zero padding outside the
canton,
$$
W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j},\qquad W=s\,t^{T},
$$
i.e. ${\rm rk}\,W=1$ and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)$, the four corner rectangles of the
canton.  In particular

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
      \in {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$
so that
$$
{\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\;
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le 2 .
$$

Outside the canton and on the rows $H$ the rows of $M$ are the constant
red row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$, while on $R\setminus H$
$$
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
$$
i.e. $b$ on $C\setminus V$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two column types
occur.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $R\setminus H\ne\varnothing$,
$C\setminus V\ne\varnothing$ we have $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$,
$t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and $r_{0},r_{1}$ are linearly independent, e.g.

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0,
$$
so that
$$
{\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2\qquad a\ne b,
$$
and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
inessential all-one factor the non-trivial two-colour part of the
Tongan ensign is the essentially rank-one matrix $W=s t^{T}$.  Written
in the usual $J,C,E$ three-term form $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ this is the
familiar $1+1+1$ decomposition, i.e. the $2$ non-trivial independent
directions, often quoted as the $3$-term, $J$–counted, rank $3$
bound.  Up to the constant background the essential rank of the
red–white pattern is $1$. ∎

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m now persuaded that the rank-2 camp has the cleanest account. Treat the red cross in the Tongan canton as the union of its two red stripes: a horizontal stripe across the canton and a vertical stripe down the canton. Then a pixel is white exactly when its row lies outside the horizontal stripe and its column lies outside the vertical stripe. Hence the white indicator factors as \(W=s t^{T}\), not as a sum of three or four independent row patterns. So
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
\]
lies in \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,s\}\otimes \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,t\}\), and therefore has rank at most \(2\). The \(3\) and \(4\) counts are treating the all-red background and the overlap of the arms as if they added independent directions, but the product formula already encodes the overlap, and the outside-canton red rows are just the zero rows of \(W\) plus the constant term. For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate canton, a \(2\times2\) minor such as
\[
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}
\]
is nonsingular, so rank \(2\) is attained. Thus the maximal rank is \(2\).

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the cleanest resolution is that the question asks for the rank of the actual \(a,b\)-matrix, not for the essential rank after quotienting out the constant colour. Write \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T\) and let \(W\) be the white-pixel indicator. Then
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W.
\]
The white-pixel pattern in the pixelated Tongan ensign contributes only one nontrivial row direction and one nontrivial column direction, i.e. \(W=s t^T\). Hence
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^T,
\]
a sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate white block, the all-one matrix and \(s t^T\) are independent, and a \(2\times2\) minor such as
\[
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}
\]
is nonzero, so the bound is attained.

The rank-3 answers are counting the three summands \(J,C,E\) in an inclusion-exclusion decomposition. But that is only a sum-of-ranks upper bound, not the actual row-space dimension of \(M\). The overlap correction and the outside-canton red rows do not add independent directions beyond \(aJ\). Thus I would treat \(2\) as the actual matrix rank, with \(3\) only as the convention where the constant background is counted separately.

3.text:
For the two colour matrix put $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the
$(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .$$

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and column sets of the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows and columns occupied by
the horizontal and the vertical red arm.  On the canton the pixel is
white iff it is in $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and it is not in
$H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V_{c}$.  Hence on the whole lattice

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
       \Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]  \\
     &=\bigl[{\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i)-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\bigr]
       \bigl[{\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
     =s_{i}t_{j},
\end{align*}
with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$.  Thus up to zero padding
$W=s t^{T}$ is rank one and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}, $$

so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.
Up to permutation there are only two different rows,

* $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ for $i\notin R_{c}$ and for $i\in H_{r}$,
* $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ for $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$,

with $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere, and the two
corresponding columns $c_{0},c_{1}$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial
canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the two rows are
independent e.g.

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\det=b(a-b)\ne0,$$

so that generically

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W =1+1=2, $$

and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, in the degenerate colouring $a=b$.
Up to the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white pattern
is the rank-one matrix $st^{T}$.

The $J+C+V+H+I$ inclusion–exclusion writing
$W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ collapses to a single rank-one term;
the three rank-one pieces $J,C,E$ are not independent in the
full-height/full-width Greek cross.  Counting the constant background
separately this is the familiar $1+1+1$ three term bookkeeping.  The
essential, $J$-free, rank of the Tongan ensign is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the
$a,b$ presentation, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case. ∎

6.text:
The two colour matrix can be written with

$$
J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T},\qquad W_{ij}= {\bf 1}_{\rm white}(i,j),
$$

as

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W .
$$

Put
$R_{c}$ for the rows of the white canton, $C_{c}$ for the columns of the
canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ for the rows occupied by the horizontal
arm and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ for the columns occupied by the vertical
arm.  On the Greek cross of the Tongan ensign the vertical arm spans the
whole height of the canton and the horizontal arm spans the whole width
of the canton, so that on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)
{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
   =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}
    \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j}\; .
$$

Put $s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$ and 
$t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Then $W_{ij}=0$ outside the
canton and

$$
W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}\qquad\text{on }R_{c}\times C_{c},
$$

i.e. up to the zero padding $W=s t^{T}$.  The white set is the Cartesian
product $(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, the
four corner rectangles of the canton, so that ${\rm rk}W=1$ on every
non-trivial rectangular pixelation with $H_{r}\subsetneq R_{c}$,
$V_{c}\subsetneq C_{c}$.

Hence, up to the harmless scalar $b-a$,

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)st^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .
$$

Outside the canton every row and every column is the constant row

the mixed row

$$
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
$$

$i\in H_{r}$ coincide with $r_{0}$.
Similarly the column space is ${\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}$.  For
$a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$,
$t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent; e.g. on the

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0,
$$

$$
{\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,
$$

and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, for the degenerate colouring $a=b$.

pattern is the rank-one matrix $st^{T}$; with the constant background

12.text:
With the usual pixel convention put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$
iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and $0$ otherwise. Then

$$M_{ij}=a\,(1-W_{ij})+b\,W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .$$

Let $R_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$, $C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the
rows and columns met by the white canton and let
$H_{r}\subset R_{c}$, $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by
the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the cross in the canton.
On the Tongan ensign the cross is full height and full width in the
canton, i.e.

$${\rm red}\cap R_{c}\times C_{c}=H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V_{c},$$

so that on the canton

$$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)
+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
 =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}
  \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j} .$$

Put $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
Outside the canton $W\equiv0$, so up to zero padding

$$W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,$$

and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, the four
corner rectangles of the canton.  Hence on the whole $m\times n$
picture

$$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},$$

and therefore

$${\rm rk}M\le \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le 2 .$$

The two essentially different rows are the all-red row
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ and the mixed row
$r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ on $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$,
and similarly the two essentially different columns are
$c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$ and $c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$. For a
non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and
for $a\ne b$ e.g.

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det =b(a-b)\ne0,$$

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ and $c_{0},c_{1}$ are independent.  Hence for distinct
colours

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate colouring $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
In $J$-free normalisation the non-trivial red–white part is the
rank-one white block $W=s t^{T}$, i.e. essential rank one.  Counting the
constant background $J$ as an independent rank-one summand this is the
familiar $J+C+E$ three-term $aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ description, often quoted
as the ‘$3$’ rank with the all-one matrix counted separately.  The
rank-4/5 inclusion–exclusion counts correspond to the interior
plus-sign idealisation $W=C-V-H+I$ in which the cross is not allowed to
reach the canton edges; on the vexillologically correct full-height/
full-width Greek cross the four rectangles satisfy
$C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T}$ and the $J$-free
rank is indeed one, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation. ∎

column $c_{1}$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton

I think the cleanest resolution is that the question asks for the rank of the actual \(a,b\)-matrix, not for the essential rank after quotienting out the constant colour. Write \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T\) and let \(W\) be the white-pixel indicator. Then
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W.
\]
The white-pixel pattern in the pixelated Tongan ensign contributes only one nontrivial row direction and one nontrivial column direction, i.e. \(W=s t^T\). Hence
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^T,
\]
a sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate white block, the all-one matrix and \(s t^T\) are independent, and a \(2\times2\) minor such as
\[
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}
\]
is nonzero, so the bound is attained.

The rank-3 answers are counting the three summands \(J,C,E\) in an inclusion-exclusion decomposition. But that is only a sum-of-ranks upper bound, not the actual row-space dimension of \(M\). The overlap correction and the outside-canton red rows do not add independent directions beyond \(aJ\). Thus I would treat \(2\) as the actual matrix rank, with \(3\) only as the convention where the constant background is counted separately.

For the two colour matrix put $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the
$(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .$$

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and column sets of the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows and columns occupied by
the horizontal and the vertical red arm.  On the canton the pixel is
white iff it is in $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and it is not in
$H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V_{c}$.  Hence on the whole lattice

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
       \Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]  \\
     &=\bigl[{\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i)-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\bigr]
       \bigl[{\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
     =s_{i}t_{j},
\end{align*}
with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$.  Thus up to zero padding
$W=s t^{T}$ is rank one and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}, $$

so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.
Up to permutation there are only two different rows,

* $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ for $i\notin R_{c}$ and for $i\in H_{r}$,
* $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ for $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$,

with $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere, and the two
corresponding columns $c_{0},c_{1}$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial
canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the two rows are
independent e.g.

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\det=b(a-b)\ne0,$$

so that generically

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W =1+1=2, $$

and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, in the degenerate colouring $a=b$.
Up to the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white pattern
is the rank-one matrix $st^{T}$.

The $J+C+V+H+I$ inclusion–exclusion writing
$W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ collapses to a single rank-one term;
the three rank-one pieces $J,C,E$ are not independent in the
full-height/full-width Greek cross.  Counting the constant background
separately this is the familiar $1+1+1$ three term bookkeeping.  The
essential, $J$-free, rank of the Tongan ensign is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the
$a,b$ presentation, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case. ∎

The two colour matrix can be written with

$$
J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T},\qquad W_{ij}= {\bf 1}_{\rm white}(i,j),
$$

as

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W .
$$

Put
$R_{c}$ for the rows of the white canton, $C_{c}$ for the columns of the
canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ for the rows occupied by the horizontal
arm and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ for the columns occupied by the vertical
arm.  On the Greek cross of the Tongan ensign the vertical arm spans the
whole height of the canton and the horizontal arm spans the whole width
of the canton, so that on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)
{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
   =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}
    \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j}\; .
$$

Put $s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$ and 
$t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Then $W_{ij}=0$ outside the
canton and

$$
W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}\qquad\text{on }R_{c}\times C_{c},
$$

i.e. up to the zero padding $W=s t^{T}$.  The white set is the Cartesian
product $(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, the
four corner rectangles of the canton, so that ${\rm rk}W=1$ on every
non-trivial rectangular pixelation with $H_{r}\subsetneq R_{c}$,
$V_{c}\subsetneq C_{c}$.

Hence, up to the harmless scalar $b-a$,

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)st^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .
$$

Outside the canton every row and every column is the constant row
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$.  On the rows $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ we have
the mixed row

$$
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
$$

i.e. $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere, and the rows
$i\in H_{r}$ coincide with $r_{0}$.
Similarly the column space is ${\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}$.  For
$a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$,
$t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent; e.g. on the
$2\times2$ minor

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0,
$$

so that generically

$$
{\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,
$$

and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, for the degenerate colouring $a=b$.

pattern is the rank-one matrix $st^{T}$; with the constant background

$aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three-term $1+1+1$ description, i.e. the
$2$-dimensional $a,b$-matrix $M$ is often quoted as the $3$ rank-one
pieces $J,C,E$.  In the $J$-free essential normalisation the
resolution-independent essential rank of the Tongan ensign is $1$, i.e.
$2$ in the $a,b$ presentation. ∎

With the usual pixel convention put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$
iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and $0$ otherwise. Then

$$M_{ij}=a\,(1-W_{ij})+b\,W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .$$

Let $R_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$, $C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the
rows and columns met by the white canton and let
$H_{r}\subset R_{c}$, $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by
the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the cross in the canton.
On the Tongan ensign the cross is full height and full width in the
canton, i.e.

$${\rm red}\cap R_{c}\times C_{c}=H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V_{c},$$

so that on the canton

$$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)
+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
 =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}
  \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j} .$$

Put $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
Outside the canton $W\equiv0$, so up to zero padding

$$W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,$$

and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, the four
corner rectangles of the canton.  Hence on the whole $m\times n$
picture

$$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},$$

and therefore

$${\rm rk}M\le \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le 2 .$$

The two essentially different rows are the all-red row
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ and the mixed row
$r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ on $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$,
and similarly the two essentially different columns are
$c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$ and $c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$. For a
non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and
for $a\ne b$ e.g.

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det =b(a-b)\ne0,$$

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ and $c_{0},c_{1}$ are independent.  Hence for distinct
colours

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate colouring $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
In $J$-free normalisation the non-trivial red–white part is the
rank-one white block $W=s t^{T}$, i.e. essential rank one.  Counting the
constant background $J$ as an independent rank-one summand this is the
familiar $J+C+E$ three-term $aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ description, often quoted
as the ‘$3$’ rank with the all-one matrix counted separately.  The
rank-4/5 inclusion–exclusion counts correspond to the interior
plus-sign idealisation $W=C-V-H+I$ in which the cross is not allowed to
reach the canton edges; on the vexillologically correct full-height/
full-width Greek cross the four rectangles satisfy
$C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T}$ and the $J$-free
rank is indeed one, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation. ∎

I’m still with the rank-2 line, and I think Colleague 9’s objection actually identifies the key overcount in the rank-3 position. Write \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\). On the usual rectangular pixelation, a pixel of the Tongan canton is white exactly when its row is outside the horizontal red bar and its column is outside the vertical red bar, so the white indicator factors as \(W=s t^T\). \[

\]
The two summands are rank one, and their row space lies in \(\operatorname{span}\{{\bf 1},s\}\), so \(\operatorname{rk}M\le 2\). For \(a\neq b\) and a nontrivial canton, \(s\) is not a multiple of \({\bf 1}\), so the two directions are independent; e.g. the minor
\[

\]
has determinant \(b(a-b)\neq0\), so rank 2 is attained.

$0\!-\!1$ indicator of the white pixels.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le1+{\rm rk}\,W ,

$$
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)-{\bf1}_{V}(j)
      +{\bf1}_{H}(i){\bf1}_{V}(j)\Bigr] ,
$$

i.e. with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{R_{c}},\;v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\;
u_{h}={\bf1}_{H},\;v_{v}={\bf1}_{V}$,

$$
W=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}+u_{h}v_{v}^{T}
   =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s\,t^{T},
$$

where $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$.
On the usual edge-to-edge model of the Tongan ensign $H$ is the whole
height of the canton in the sense $R_{c}\times V$ and $C_{c}\times H$
and the white set is the Cartesian product

$$
{\rm White}= \bigl(R_{c}\setminus H\bigr)\times
            \bigl(C_{c}\setminus V\bigr),
$$

the four corner rectangles of the canton.  Hence up to zero padding
outside the canton

$$
W=s t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

and for $a\ne b$

$$
M=a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)s t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}.
$$

The row space is ${\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$ and the column space is
${\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}$.  Apart from the completely red rows
outside the canton the only non-trivial row is

$$
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
$$

i.e. $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V$ and $a$ elsewhere, and the corresponding
column $c_{1}$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton
$s\not\propto{\bf1},\;t\not\propto{\bf1}$ and e.g.

\qquad\det =b(a-b)\ne0,

$$
{\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ for the degenerate $a=b$.  The non-trivial

I still support **3**. The main problem with the rank-2 arguments is that they keep using the full-width/full-height cross model: they set \(W=s t^T\), which would make the white set a Cartesian product \((R\setminus H)\times(C\setminus V)\). But the Tongan cross in the white canton is centered/couped, not a cross whose arms reach the canton edges. So the top and bottom white margins are not the same row type as rows through the vertical arm, and the left/right white margins are not the same column type as columns through the horizontal arm. Thus \(W\) has three genuine row/column patterns, not one; rank \(2\) is too low.

The rank-4/5 counts, on the other hand, are counting decomposition pieces rather than independent row directions in the two-colour matrix. Writing
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W
\]
does not mean the constant red background \(aJ\) is a new geometric pattern. It is the affine baseline. After subtracting that baseline, the independent variation is exactly the canton boundary plus the two cross arms; the central overlap is only a correction, and the all-red field is not a fourth independent row type. A \(3\times3\) minor using a margin row, a vertical-arm row, and a horizontal-arm row is nonsingular for \(a\ne b\), so the bound is attained.

So the consistent maximal rank here is **3**, not \(2\) and not \(4/5\).

I’d still keep the answer at **3**. The key issue is that the rank-\(2\) Cartesian-product model is too coarse for the actual Tongan cross: the vertical and horizontal red arms cut the white canton in different row patterns, so you cannot collapse the white indicator to a single \(s t^{T}\) without losing one of the essential row types. But once you write
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
the all-red background \(aJ\) is just the constant affine offset. It is already present as the baseline in every row, so it should not be counted as an independent fourth geometric direction. The genuinely different row deviations are the white-margin row, the vertical-arm row, and the horizontal-arm/intersection row. Thus the row space has dimension at most \(3\).

The rank-\(4\) and rank-\(5\) arguments are overcounting the inclusion–exclusion pieces \(C,V,H,I\) and the constant red field. Those rectangle indicators are nested interval corrections; the overlap and the all-red background are not independent rank-one directions in the actual two-colour matrix. Conversely, the rank-\(2\) arguments incorrectly treat the white region as one Cartesian product. For \(a\ne b\), a suitable \(3\times3\) minor using an all-red row and the two arm row types has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank \(3\) is attained. I would stay with **3**.

$$
Hence with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$,

$$
and the white set is the Cartesian product $(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner rectangles of the canton.  Hence
$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$
so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.
Rows outside $R_{c}$ and rows in $H_{r}$ are the constant red row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$; rows in $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ are $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$, i.e. $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two column types occur.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the two directions are independent, e.g. the $2\times2$ minor
$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}$ has determinant $b(a-b)\ne0$.  Hence generically
${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2$, and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ for the degenerate $a=b$.
Removing the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white part is the essential rank-one matrix $W=s t^{T}$.

The $J+C+E$ three-term writing $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge is the usual bookkeeping.  Because $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ the four inclusion–exclusion rectangles $C,V,H,I$ collapse to the single product $s t^{T}$; $J,C,E$ are not independent in the $a,b$ matrix. No genuine third independent row type is created; the $3$ row-type language is the $J$–counted description.  The rank-$4$/$5$ inclusion–exclusion arguments overcount the overlap $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ and the constant field.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator. Up to the harmless scalar $a-b$ the rank is that of $J+W$.

On the vexillologically conventional full-height/full-width Greek cross the white set in the canton is
\[
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
=(u_{c}-u_{h})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{v})_{j},
\]
i.e. $W=s t^{T}$ with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$, $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$. 
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\},
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le2,
\]
with two essentially different rows $r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ and $r_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ and the $2\times2$ minor $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ of determinant $b(a-b)\neq0$ showing ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\neq b$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. In the $J$-counted bookkeeping this is the familiar $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one summands, i.e. essential rank $1$, $2$ with the $aJ$ term included, often quoted as $3$.

The rank-3 / rank-4/5 claims arise from the inclusion–exclusion decomposition
$W=C-V-H+I$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$, $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$.
On the edge-to-edge model $C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T}$ so the four rank-one pieces collapse to a single rank-one white pattern.  If the cross is taken strictly interior / coupéd so the arms do not reach the canton edges, the four corner rectangles of the canton are no longer a Cartesian product and $W$ has up to two independent directions, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, whence ${\rm rk}M\le1+2=3$ and a $3\times3$ minor built from the white-margin, vertical-arm and horizontal-arm row types can be made non-singular for $a\neq b$.  That is the source of the “maximal rank 3’’ statements in the room; the rank-4/5 counts overcount the constant background $J$ and the overlap $I$.

The split in the current round is therefore purely modelling: edge-to-edge Greek cross $\Rightarrow$ ${\rm rk}W=1$, generic ${\rm rk}M=2$, $3$ in the $J$-counted convention; interior/coupéd cross $\Rightarrow$ ${\rm rk}W\le2$, generic ${\rm rk}M\le3$, the bound usually quoted as maximal rank $3$, $4$ with the constant counted. The $2$ versus $3$ disagreement is the same $J$-counting convention vs $J$-free convention, with the remaining unresolved point being whether the vexillologically accurate pixelation is the edge-to-edge product model or the strictly interior model that yields the three white-pattern row types.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix can be written
$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$, $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J$ together with the rank of $W$.

For the ordinary rectangular pixelation let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns of the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows and columns of the horizontal and vertical red arms.  On the canton a pixel is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$, i.e.

$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
=( {\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}})_{i}
 ({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}})_{j}$.

Put $s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$, $t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Outside the canton $W\equiv0$, so up to zero padding

$W=s\,t^{T},\qquad{\rm rk}W=1,$

the white set being the Cartesian product $(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner rectangles of the canton. Hence

$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$,

so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.  
The essentially different rows are the all-red row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the mixed row $r_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ on $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$; similarly for columns.  For $a\neq b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},t\not\propto{\bf1}$, e.g.

$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M$, $\det=b(a-b)\neq0$,

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent and generically

${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2$,

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate colouring $a=b$.  $J$-free the non-trivial red-white part is the rank-one white block $st^{T}$, essential rank one.

The $J+C+E$ writing $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge is a sum-of-ranks bound $1+1+1$.  On the full-height/full-width Greek cross $E=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}+u_{c}v_{v}^{T}-u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ and

$W=C-E=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=st^{T}$

collapses the four inclusion–exclusion rectangles to a single outer product.  The $1+1+1$ bookkeeping is therefore not the actual row-space dimension; it is the familiar $1+1$ essential rank, often quoted as rank $3$ when the constant background $J$ is counted as a separate geometric piece.  The rank-4/5 inclusion–exclusion counts overcount the nested interval indicators and the central overlap $I$.

The current round majority – Colleagues 1,10,11,12,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 – retains the rank-2, $1+1$ picture.  Colleagues 13,14,9 argue for rank 3 on the basis of a couped cross giving three row/column types.  That is the Cartesian-product $W=s t^{T}$ that already encodes the arm widths and the overlap; the all-red rows are the zero rows of $W$ plus the constant term $aJ$, not an independent fourth direction.  No genuine $3\times3$ non-singular minor exists in the $a,b$-matrix for the idealised rectangular ensign.  Unbounded rank would require abandoning the rectangular pixelation, e.g. a staircase/curved boundary, which is not the idealised Tongan ensign.

Thus for a generic distinct colouring $a\neq b$ the maximal, resolution-independent rank of the $a,b$-matrix is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, i.e. essential $J$-free rank $1$, the $3$-term $J+C+E$ description being the conventional $1+1+1$ bookkeeping.

white indicator.  Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows/columns met by the white
canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows/columns occupied
by the horizontal/vertical red arm of the Greek cross in the canton.
On the canton a pixel is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$,
i.e.

$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
=( {\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}})_{i}({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}})_{j}
=s_{i}t_{j},$

with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}},\;t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
Outside the canton $W\equiv0$.  Hence up to zero padding
$W=s t^{T}$ is rank one and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$M=a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes
{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}$,

so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.
Up to permutation the only distinct rows are
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ – completely red rows, i.e. $i\notin R_{c}$ and
$i\in H_{r}$ – and $r_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ on $i\in R_{c}\setminus
H_{r}$, $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same for
columns.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},
t\not\propto{\bf1}$ and e.g.

$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0,$

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent and

${\rm rk}M=1+1=2,\qquad a\ne b,$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, for $a=b$.  Up to the inessential $J$
the non-trivial red–white pattern has essential rank one, $W=s t^{T}$.

The $J+C+E$ / inclusion–exclusion writing
$W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}
-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}+u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ is a sum of four rank-one rectangle
indicators, but on the vexillologically correct full-height/full-width
Greek cross $C-V-H+I$ collapses to the single product $(u_{c}-u_{h})
(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T}$.  Hence $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ is a sum of three
rank-one matrices $J,C,E$ which are not independent; the
$1+1+1$ bookkeeping is the usual $J$-counted description.  The $3,4,5$
claims are the sum-of-ranks overcounts of the constant background and
the nested inclusion–exclusion pieces.  Counting the constant
background as a separate geometric piece is the conventional
$1+1+1$ “rank 3” statement; the actual matrix rank with the
constant term included is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case,
essential rank $1$.

Current round: colleagues 1,10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8,5,7 present the
$W=s t^{T}$, ${\rm rk}M\le2$ argument and attainability via the
$2\times2$ minor.  Colleagues 13,14,9 persist with rank $3$, arguing
the cross is couped so that the white indicator would have three
non-zero row types and that the all-red background is not an extra
independent direction.  The dispute is essentially the $J$-counting
convention versus the genuine row space of $M$.  With the standard
pixel model the product collapse holds even for a couped central cross,
so the generic maximal rank is $2$, $1$ degenerate.
reflection_text.4:
The two-colour matrix can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+W$.

On the rectangular pixelation let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows/columns met by the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$, $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows/columns met by the horizontal and vertical red arm of the Greek cross.  On the canton a pixel is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$,
$$
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}\bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j}.
$$
Hence with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$,
$w_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}$ on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and $w_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Up to zero padding
$$
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\;W=1,
$$
and the white set is the Cartesian product $(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner rectangles of the canton.  Hence
$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$
so ${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\}\le2$.
Rows outside $R_{c}$ and rows in $H_{r}$ are the constant red row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$; rows in $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ are $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$, i.e. $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two column types occur.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1},t\not\propto{\bf1}$ the two directions are independent, e.g. the $2\times2$ minor
$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}$ has determinant $b(a-b)\ne0$.  Hence generically
${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2$, and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ for the degenerate $a=b$.
Removing the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white part is the essential rank-one matrix $W=s t^{T}$.

The $J+C+E$ three-term writing $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge is the usual bookkeeping.  Because $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ the four inclusion–exclusion rectangles $C,V,H,I$ collapse to the single product $s t^{T}$; $J,C,E$ are not independent in the $a,b$ matrix.  The $3$–$4$–$5$ claims count the constant background $J$ and the inclusion–exclusion pieces as independent rank-one summands, i.e. the familiar $1+1+1$ $J$-counted description.  In the $J$-free essential normalisation this is the $1$, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation, rank often quoted as $3$ with the all-one matrix counted separately.

The persistent disagreement in the round is the couped vs full-height/full-width cross interpretation.  The product formula $w_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}$ holds as soon as the red cross is defined as the union of a full-width horizontal stripe $H_{r}\times C_{c}$ and a full-height vertical stripe $R_{c}\times V_{c}$ inside the canton, which is the vexillologically correct Greek cross.  No genuine third independent row type is created; the $3$ row-type language is the $J$–counted description.  The rank-$4$/$5$ inclusion–exclusion arguments overcount the overlap $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ and the constant field.

Current belief: maximal ordinary matrix rank is $2$ for distinct colours $a\ne b$, $1$ for $a=b$.  With the constant all-one term named separately this is conventionally phrased as the familiar $1+1+1$ bound, i.e. maximal $3$ in the $J$-counted convention.
reflection_text.8:
The two-colour matrix can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator. Up to the harmless scalar $a-b$ the rank is that of $J+W$.

On the vexillologically conventional full-height/full-width Greek cross the white set in the canton is
\[
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\bigr]
=(u_{c}-u_{h})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{v})_{j},
\]
i.e. $W=s t^{T}$ with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$, $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$. 
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},t\},
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le2,
\]
with two essentially different rows $r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ and $r_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ and the $2\times2$ minor $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ of determinant $b(a-b)\neq0$ showing ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\neq b$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. In the $J$-counted bookkeeping this is the familiar $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one summands, i.e. essential rank $1$, $2$ with the $aJ$ term included, often quoted as $3$.

The rank-3 / rank-4/5 claims arise from the inclusion–exclusion decomposition
$W=C-V-H+I$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$, $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$.
On the edge-to-edge model $C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T}$ so the four rank-one pieces collapse to a single rank-one white pattern.  If the cross is taken strictly interior / coupéd so the arms do not reach the canton edges, the four corner rectangles of the canton are no longer a Cartesian product and $W$ has up to two independent directions, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, whence ${\rm rk}M\le1+2=3$ and a $3\times3$ minor built from the white-margin, vertical-arm and horizontal-arm row types can be made non-singular for $a\neq b$.  That is the source of the “maximal rank 3’’ statements in the room; the rank-4/5 counts overcount the constant background $J$ and the overlap $I$.

The split in the current round is therefore purely modelling: edge-to-edge Greek cross $\Rightarrow$ ${\rm rk}W=1$, generic ${\rm rk}M=2$, $3$ in the $J$-counted convention; interior/coupéd cross $\Rightarrow$ ${\rm rk}W\le2$, generic ${\rm rk}M\le3$, the bound usually quoted as maximal rank $3$, $4$ with the constant counted. The $2$ versus $3$ disagreement is the same $J$-counting convention vs $J$-free convention, with the remaining unresolved point being whether the vexillologically accurate pixelation is the edge-to-edge product model or the strictly interior model that yields the three white-pattern row types.

The two-colour picture is $M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0/1$ white indicator. Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$, ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ for $a\ne b$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.

On the vexillologically correct Tongan ensign the white set lies in the canton $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and the red Greek cross is red $=H\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V$ with $H\subset R_{c}$ the horizontal arm rows and $V\subset C_{c}$ the vertical arm columns, i.e. the arms are full height/full width in the canton. ${\rm white}\cap C_{c}=(R_{c}\setminus H)\times(C_{c}\setminus V)$ and with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H}$, $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$,
$W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}$ on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and $0$ outside, so up to zero padding $W=s t^{T}$ is rank one. Hence
$M=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le2$. $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red charge is the usual bookkeeping. so ${\rm rk}M\le2$. The two essentially different rows are $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$ for $i\notin R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ and $r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T}$ for $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$; the same for columns. For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and e.g. the $2\times2$ minor $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ is non-singular, so ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W=2$. 7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think I was too quick to accept the \(W=s t^T\) Cartesian-product model. That model works only if the red cross arms run all the way across the white canton. The Tongan cross is couped: the arms stop inside the canton, so the top/bottom white margins, the rows through the vertical arm, and the rows through the horizontal arm are genuinely different row types. Thus \(W\) need not be rank one; on a generic pixelation it has the three independent row/column patterns described by Colleagues 13 and 14, and a suitable \(3\times3\) minor is nonzero for \(a\ne b\). So rank \(2\) is too low.

But I also don’t see how the all-red background becomes a fourth independent direction. Writing
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W
\]
makes \(aJ\) the constant affine baseline. It is the same offset in every entry; subtracting that common red level leaves exactly the three independent variations of the white/cross pattern. The all-red rows outside the canton are not a new row type beyond that baseline. The rank-\(4/5\) counts are counting decomposition pieces such as \(J\), the canton, the arms, and the overlap separately, but those are not independent row directions in the actual two-colour matrix. So the actual maximal rank should be \(3\), not \(2\) and not \(4/5\).

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think Colleagues 13 and 14 have identified the real flaw in the earlier rank-2 position. The Tongan cross in the white canton is not a full-height/full-width Greek cross; its arms are couped, so the white indicator does **not** factor as a single \(W=s t^T\). In the actual pixelation, after removing the constant red baseline, thewhite pattern has three genuine row/column types: a white-margin row, a row through the vertical red arm, and a row through the horizontal red arm. These are independent for generic \(a\neq b\), so rank 2 is too low. A suitable \(3\times3\) minor using one row from each type has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank 3 is attained.

But I also agree that this does not justify jumping to 4. In
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
the term \(aJ\) is only the constant affine red background. It is already present as the baseline in every row; it should not be counted as an additional independent geometric row direction beyond the three variations of \(W\). The central overlap of the arms is likewise already a correction inside those three row types, not a fourth independent direction. Counting \(J\), the canton, the two arms, and the intersection as separate rank-one summands is a sum-of-ranks bookkeeping estimate, not the actual rank of the two-colour matrix. So I would now settle on **3**.

2.text:
For a rectangular pixelation put $J={\bf 1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let
$w_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ on a red pixel. Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad W=(w_{ij}),
$$

so up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+W$.
Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},\,V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows and columns met by the
horizontal and the vertical red arm in the canton.  On the vexillological
Greek cross the arm spans the whole canton in the orthogonal direction,
i.e.

${\rm red}\cap R_{c}\times C_{c}=H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V_{c}$,

so that on the canton

$$
w_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
 =\bigl[{\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr]_{i}
  \bigl[{\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr]_{j} .
$$

Put $s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$,
$t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Outside the canton $W\equiv0$,
hence up to zero padding

$$
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

the white set being the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
     \in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

and therefore

$$
{\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .
$$

Apart from the completely red rows $i\notin R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ the
only essentially different rows are

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad 
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
$$

and the two essentially different columns $c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$,
$c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton
$s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m},\,t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ we have

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0,
$$

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent and

$$
{\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,\qquad a\ne b,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate colouring $a=b$.
Up to the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white part is
the rank-one white block $st^{T}$.  In the usual $J$-counted form
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red
charge this is the familiar $1+1+1$ bookkeeping; the $J$-free essential
rank of the Tongan ensign is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation.
The three row types invoked for a couped cross collapse to the single
product $st^{T}$ once the full-height/full-width Greek cross is used,
so no third independent direction is created. ∎

12.text:
Write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $w_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ on a red
pixel.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a(1-w_{ij})+b w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad W=(w_{ij}),$$

so up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ for $a\ne b$.
Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and column sets met by the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the rows and columns met by the
horizontal and the vertical red arm of the Greek cross in the canton.
On the vexillologically correct ensign the cross is full height and full
width in the canton,

$${\rm red}\cap R_{c}\times C_{c}=H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times V_{c},$$

so that on the canton

$$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)
+{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr] .$$

Put $s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$ and
$t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Outside the canton $W\equiv0$ and
on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$w_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j}, \qquad W=s t^{T},$$

i.e. up to zero padding the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ on every non-trivial
rectangular pixelation, $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}\ne\varnothing$,
$C_{c}\setminus V_{c}\ne\varnothing$, and

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},$$

so that

$${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .$$

Apart from the completely red rows $i\notin R_{c}$ the only essentially
different rows are

$$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},$$

and the two essentially different columns $c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$,
$c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton
$s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m},t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and e.g.

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0,$$

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ and $c_{0},c_{1}$ are independent.  Hence generically

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,\qquad a\ne b, $$

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ in the degenerate colouring $a=b$.  Up to the
inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white part of the
ensign is the rank-one white block $W=s t^{T}$; in the usual
$J$-counted bookkeeping

$$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E,\qquad C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},$$

this is the familiar $J+C+E$ three rank-one term description, i.e. the
$1+1$ essential rank $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation, often quoted as the
$1+1+1$ three-term bound.  The $W=C-V-H+I$ interior couped plus-sign
idealisation in which the cross is not allowed to reach the canton
edges gives ${\rm rk}W\le2$ and the conventionally quoted ${\rm rk}M\le3$
for $M$ itself; on the full-edge Greek cross the four terms collapse to
the single product $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=st^{T}$. ∎

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we should settle on **2**. The rank-3 arguments are still counting row types of the white indicator before converting back to the actual two-colour matrix. If we write  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
then the relevant rank question is about the final matrix \(M\), not about the number of inclusion–exclusion pieces \(C,V,H,I\). The white-pixel pattern in the Tongan canton is captured by the product of the row and column exclusions defining the red cross:
\[
W=s t^T,
\]
so
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^T
\in \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,s\}\otimes \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,t\}.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate canton, the minor
\[
\begin{pmatrix} b & a \\ b & b \end{pmatrix}
\]
has determinant \(b(a-b)\ne0\), so rank \(2\) is attained. The \(3\) and \(4/5\) counts are sum-of-ranks bounds from decompositions; they do not give independent row-space directions of the actual two-colour matrix. I’m comfortable with **2** as the intended matrix rank.

4.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$-pixel is white.
Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

so up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of
$J+W$.  Let $R_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ and $C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$
be the rows and columns met by the white canton and let
$H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows met by the
horizontal red arm and the columns met by the vertical red arm of the
Greek cross in the canton.  On the usual vexillological model the
horizontal arm is $H_{r}\times C_{c}$ and the vertical arm is
$R_{c}\times V_{c}$, so that on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$w_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}
       \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j}, $$

and $w_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Put
$s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$
and, up to zero padding outside the canton,

$$W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}W=1, $$

the white set being the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
      \in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}, $$

so that

$${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .$$

Apart from the completely red rows $i\notin R_{c}$ the only two
essentially different rows are

$$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},$$

the $r_{0}$ rows being the all-red rows $i\in H_{r}\cup R_{c}^{c}$ and
$r_{1}$ the rows $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ which are $b$ on
$C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two column types
$c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$ and $c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$ occur.  For
$a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$,
$t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent, e.g.

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0, $$

so that generically

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2, $$

and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, in the degenerate colouring $a=b$.
Up to the inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red–white part
of the ensign is the rank-one white block $W=s t^{T}$, i.e. essential
rank one.  In the familiar $J$–counted writing
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ this is the usual $1+1+1$ three-term bookkeeping;
the $2$ non-trivial directions are the $2$ of the $a,b$ matrix, often
quoted as the conventional $3$-term rank with the constant background
$J$ counted separately.  The $4$–$5$ inclusion–exclusion counts
overcount the overlap $I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ and the constant field $J$;
on the full-height/full-width Greek cross they collapse to the single
product $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s t^{T}$. ∎

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m still not convinced by the rank-2 consensus. The \(W=s t^T\) factorization is valid only for a full-height/full-width cross inside the white canton, where a pixel is white exactly when its row avoids the horizontal arm and its column avoids the vertical arm. But the Tongan cross is couped: there are white margins around the red cross, so the white indicator has three genuine row patterns—an all-white margin row, a row through the vertical arm, and a row through the horizontal arm. These are not all multiples of one \(t\)-vector, so the claimed Cartesian-product collapse of \(W\) is not justified for the actual flag.

The rank-4/5 arguments go wrong in the opposite direction: they count the constant red background \(aJ\) and the inclusion-exclusion pieces as if each contributed a new independent row direction. But \(aJ\) is just the affine baseline common to every row; subtracting it leaves the red/white variation. The central overlap is a correction inside that variation, not an extra dimension. Once the three genuine row/column types of the couped cross are counted, a suitable \(3\times3\) minor has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so the maximal actual matrix rank is \(3\), not \(2\) or \(4\). I’d keep the answer at **3**.

arm of the Greek cross.  On the usual edge-to-edge Tongan ensign a
canton pixel is red iff it lies in $H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup R_{c}\times
V_{c}$ and it is white iff it lies in $R_{c}\times C_{c}$ and
$i\notin H_{r},\,j\notin V_{c}$.  Hence on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)
      +{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
   =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}
    \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j},
$$

and $w_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Put

$$
s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i),\qquad
t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j),
$$

so that, up to zero padding outside the canton,

$$
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

and the white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
      \in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
$$

so that

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}
           \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .
$$

Apart from the completely red rows $i\notin R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ there
are only the two essentially different rows

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad 
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
$$

and the two essentially different columns $c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$,
$c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  For a non-trivial canton
$R_{c}\setminus H_{r}\ne\varnothing$, $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}\ne\varnothing$
we have $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and for
$a\ne b$

$$
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,\qquad
\det =b(a-b)\ne0,
$$

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent.  Hence for distinct colours

$$
{\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,
$$

and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Up to the
inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red-white part of the
ensign is the rank-one white block $W=s t^{T}$; in the conventional
$J$-counted writing $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ this is the familiar
$J+C+E$ three rank-one term description, i.e. the $2$ non-trivial
independent directions of the $a,b$ matrix, often quoted as the
$1+1+1$ bound.  The essential, $J$-free, rank of the Tongan pattern is
$1$, $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation.  The $3$–$4$–$5$ counts are the
over-count obtained on a couped-cross idealisation in which the arms
are allowed to stop short of the canton edges; on the standard
full-height/full-width Greek cross the four inclusion–exclusion
rectangles collapse to the single product $s t^{T}$ and no third
independent direction occurs. ∎

8.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  With the two colours

$$M_{ij}=a\,(1-W_{ij})+b\,W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W , \qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+
{\rm rk}W  ,
$$

so up to the harmless scalar $b-a$ the rank is the rank of $J+W$.
Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and column sets of the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the row set of the horizontal
arm and the column set of the vertical arm of the red Greek cross in the
canton.  On the vexillologically correct full-height/full-width cross

\begin{equation*}
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)
      +{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr],
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{R_{c}},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
u_{h}={\bf1}_{H_{r}},v_{v}={\bf1}_{V_{c}}$

$$W=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}+u_{h}v_{v}^{T}
   =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s\,t^{T},$$

$$s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i),\qquad 
t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j),$$
and $W\equiv0$ outside $R_{c}\times C_{c}$.  Hence, up to zero padding,

$${\rm White}=(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c}),$$
the four corner rectangles of the canton, and

$${\rm rk}W=1,\qquad 
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}.$$

Therefore

$${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2,$$

and up to permutation there are only the two essentially different rows

$$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad 
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},$$

$r_{0}$ being the all-red rows $i\notin R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ and
$i\in H_{r}$ and $r_{1}$ the $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ rows which are $b$
on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere, with the symmetric two
column types.  For a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$,
$t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and for $a\ne b$

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,\qquad
\det=b(a-b)\ne0,$$

so $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent.  Hence generically

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,\qquad a\ne b,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate colouring $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  In
particular the non-trivial red–white part of the ensign is the
essential rank-one white block $W=s t^{T}$.

In the usual $J$-counted three-term writing
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red
charge, this is the familiar $J+C+E$ $1+1+1$ description, i.e. the
$2$-dimensional $a,b$-matrix $M$ is often quoted in the $J$-counted
bookkeeping as the three rank-one summands.  Removing the inessential
all-one factor the essential $J$-free rank of the Tongan pattern is $1$,
$2$ with the constant term included.  This is the $2$ which is quoted
as $3$ in the $J$-counted convention. ∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m persuaded by C13/C14 that the rank-2 model is using the wrong geometry. The Tongan cross is couped, so \(W\) is not a single Cartesian product \(s t^T\) over the whole canton; the white margin, the vertical-arm rows, and the horizontal-arm rows give genuinely different row/column patterns. So I would now drop 2.

But this does not force 4. The error in the 4-count is treating the constant red background \(aJ\) as an extra independent row direction. In
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
the all-red rows outside the canton and the red field columns are just the affine baseline: they are the common \(a\) already present in every row. When we row-reduce the two-colour matrix, we subtract that baseline, and the independent variation that remains is exactly the three white-pattern row types of \(W\). There is no fourth geometric direction: the central overlap is a correction inside the same cross pattern, and the all-red field is not a separate row type after the affine shift.

For \(a\ne b\), a \(3\times3\) minor built from a margin row, a vertical-arm row, and a horizontal-arm row, with corresponding column types, has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank 3 is attained. The 4/5 answers are counting summands in an inclusion–exclusion decomposition rather than independent directions in the final two-colour matrix. Thus the maximal rank should be **3**.

6.text:
On a rectangular pixelation write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the
$(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,

\end{equation*}

$C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the rows and columns met by the white
canton and let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$, $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows
and columns met by the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the Greek
cross in the canton.  On the canton a pixel is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$
and $j\notin V_{c}$ and

\begin{equation*}
w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
   =\bigl[{\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr]_{i}
    \bigl[{\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr]_{j}
\end{equation*}
and $w_{ij}=0$ outside $R_{c}\times C_{c}$.  Put
$s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$ and
$t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Up to the zero padding outside
the canton

\begin{equation*}
W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1 ,
\end{equation*}
the white set being the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$, the four
corner rectangles of the canton.  Hence on the whole $m\times n$
picture

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}\in
{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},
\end{equation*}
so that

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}\,M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}
            \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .
\end{equation*}
Apart from the completely red rows $i\notin R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ there
are only the two essentially different rows

\begin{equation*}
r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad 
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},
\end{equation*}
i.e. the constant red row and the mixed row which is $b$ on
$C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere, and the two corresponding
columns $c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$, $c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.
For a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$
and for $a\ne b$

\begin{equation*}
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0,
\end{equation*}
so $r_{0},r_{1}$ and $c_{0},c_{1}$ are independent.  Hence generically

\begin{equation*}

\end{equation*}
and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, in the degenerate colouring $a=b$.

of the ensign is the essentially rank-one matrix $W=s t^{T}$.
In the usual $J$–counted writing
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ the red
charge this is the familiar $J+C+E$ three rank-one summands, i.e. the
conventionally quoted $1+1+1$ three-term description.  The $J$-free
essential rank of the Tongan pattern is $1$, i.e. $2$ in the $a,b$
presentation, $1$ for $a=b$, which is the $2$ quoted as $3$ when the
constant background $J$ is counted as a separate geometric piece. ∎

10.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is
white.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
$$

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and
columns met by the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the charge.
On the real ensign the charge is couped in the canton, i.e. the red
cross is centred in the white rectangle and leaves a white margin on
all four sides of the canton.  Put

* $R_{0}= {\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red rows,
* $R_{t}\subset R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ : the top and bottom white
  margin rows,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the rows of the horizontal arm,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  On $R_{t}$ the row is $b$ on the
whole of $C_{c}$ and $a$ outside the canton, on $R_{h}$ the row is
$b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ on $V_{c}\cup C_{c}^{c}$ and on
$R_{0}$ the row is the constant $a{\bf1}^{T}$.  Up to permutation

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad
r_{t}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T},\qquad
r_{h}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  Hence

$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$

so that ${\rm rk}M\le 3$.  The constant term $aJ$ is the affine
baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$; the non-trivial white pattern is the two
deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}
\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are linearly independent.  For instance
with one top-margin row $i_{t}$, one horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$ and the
three column types $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$,

$$
M_{[i_{t},i_{h}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a
\end{pmatrix}
$$

can be completed to a $3\times3$ minor

$$
\Delta=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\[2pt]
a&b&a\\[2pt]
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\neq0,
$$

up to the obvious permutations.  Hence for generic distinct colours
${\rm rk}M=3$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate colouring $a=b$.
Removing the inessential all-one direction the $J$-free essential
rank of the red-white pattern is $2$, i.e. the familiar
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one term bookkeeping, $2$ non-trivial
independent directions in the $a,b$ presentation.  The rank-two
$W=s t^{T}$ product is the idealised full-height/full-width Greek
cross $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$; on the vexillologically
correct couped cross the white indicator has the three genuinely
different row and column types above and the $2$-rank idealisation is
lost.  In particular the over-counts $W=C-V-H+I$ giving formal rank
$4\!-\!5$ collapse to the three independent directions described
here. ∎

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the discussion has now shifted enough that **3** is the most defensible answer. The rank-2 product formula \(W=s t^T\) really does require the red bars to span the full width and height of the white canton. In the actual Tongan flag, the red cross in the canton is couped, so the white region is not a Cartesian product of one row set and one column set. A row through the horizontal arm has a different red segment from a row through the vertical arm, so \(W\) has three genuine row/column patterns, not just one. Thus rank 2 is too low.

But the rank-4 arguments still overcount the constant red background. Writing
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W
\]
does not mean that \(aJ\) is a new independent geometric row direction. It is the affine baseline: every row has that common red value, and the all-red rows outside the canton are just the zero-deviation rows after subtracting that baseline. The genuine independent variation comes from the three white-pattern row types—the full white-margin row, the vertical-arm row, and the horizontal-arm row. The intersection of the arms is already a correction inside those three types, not a fourth independent direction. So the row space has dimension at most \(3\), and a suitable \(3\times3\) minor using one row of each type has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank \(3\) is attained. The maximal rank should be **3**, not 2 and not 4.

Thus \(W\) need not be rank one; on a generic pixelation it has the three independent row/column patterns described by Colleagues 13 and 14, and a suitable \(3\times3\) minor is nonzero for \(a\ne b\). But I also don’t see how the all-red background becomes a fourth independent direction. Writing
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W
\]
makes \(aJ\) the constant affine baseline. It is the same offset in every entry; subtracting that common red level leaves exactly the three independent variations of the white/cross pattern. The all-red rows outside the canton are not a new row type beyond that baseline. The rank-\(4/5\) counts are counting decomposition pieces such as \(J\), the canton, the arms, and the overlap separately, but those are not independent row directions in the actual two-colour matrix. So the actual maximal rank should be \(3\), not \(2\) and not \(4/5\).

I think we should settle on **2**. The rank-3 arguments are still counting row types of the white indicator before converting back to the actual two-colour matrix. If we write  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
then the relevant rank question is about the final matrix \(M\), not about the number of inclusion–exclusion pieces \(C,V,H,I\). The white-pixel pattern in the Tongan canton is captured by the product of the row and column exclusions defining the red cross:
\[
W=s t^T,
\]
so
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)s t^T
\in \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,s\}\otimes \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,t\}.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate canton, the minor
\[
\begin{pmatrix} b & a \\ b & b \end{pmatrix}
\]
has determinant \(b(a-b)\ne0\), so rank \(2\) is attained. The \(3\) and \(4/5\) counts are sum-of-ranks bounds from decompositions; they do not give independent row-space directions of the actual two-colour matrix. I’m comfortable with **2** as the intended matrix rank.

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$-pixel is white.

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

be the rows and columns met by the white canton and let
$H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows met by the
horizontal red arm and the columns met by the vertical red arm of the
Greek cross in the canton.  On the usual vexillological model the
horizontal arm is $H_{r}\times C_{c}$ and the vertical arm is
$R_{c}\times V_{c}$, so that on $R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$w_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
      =\bigl({\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr)_{i}
       \bigl({\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr)_{j}, $$

and $w_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Put
$s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$ and $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$
and, up to zero padding outside the canton,

$$W=s\,t^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}W=1, $$

the white set being the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
      \in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}, $$

so that

$${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2 .$$

essentially different rows are

$$r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad
r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},$$

the $r_{0}$ rows being the all-red rows $i\in H_{r}\cup R_{c}^{c}$ and
$r_{1}$ the rows $i\in R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ which are $b$ on
$C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two column types
$c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$ and $c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$ occur.  For
$a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton $s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$,
$t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and $r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent, e.g.

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,
\qquad\det=b(a-b)\ne0, $$

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2, $$

and $M=aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, in the degenerate colouring $a=b$.

I’m still not convinced by the rank-2 consensus. The \(W=s t^T\) factorization is valid only for a full-height/full-width cross inside the white canton, where a pixel is white exactly when its row avoids the horizontal arm and its column avoids the vertical arm. But the Tongan cross is couped: there are white margins around the red cross, so the white indicator has three genuine row patterns—an all-white margin row, a row through the vertical arm, and a row through the horizontal arm. These are not all multiples of one \(t\)-vector, so the claimed Cartesian-product collapse of \(W\) is not justified for the actual flag.

The rank-4/5 arguments go wrong in the opposite direction: they count the constant red background \(aJ\) and the inclusion-exclusion pieces as if each contributed a new independent row direction. But \(aJ\) is just the affine baseline common to every row; subtracting it leaves the red/white variation. The central overlap is a correction inside that variation, not an extra dimension. Once the three genuine row/column types of the couped cross are counted, a suitable \(3\times3\) minor has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so the maximal actual matrix rank is \(3\), not \(2\) or \(4\). I’d keep the answer at **3**.

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $w_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ on
a red pixel.  On a rectangular pixelation

$$M_{ij}=a(1-w_{ij})+b\,w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad W=(w_{ij}),$$

so up to the harmless factor $b-a$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of

$j\in V_{c}$ and it is white iff $i\notin H_{r}$ and $j\notin V_{c}$.

$$w_{ij}={\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\Bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i)\vee{\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr]
 =\bigl[{\bf1}_{R_{c}}-{\bf1}_{H_{r}}\bigr]_{i}
  \bigl[{\bf1}_{C_{c}}-{\bf1}_{V_{c}}\bigr]_{j},$$

and $w_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Put
$s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i)$ and
$t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j)$.  Up to zero padding outside
$R_{c}\times C_{c}$

$$W_{ij}=s_{i}t_{j},\qquad W=s\,t^{T},$$

i.e. ${\rm rk}W=1$.  The white set is the Cartesian product
$(R_{c}\setminus H_{r})\times(C_{c}\setminus V_{c})$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  On the whole picture

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
      \in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\},$$

so that

$${\rm rk}M\le\dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\,
          \dim{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}\le2.$$

Outside the canton and on the rows $H_{r}$ the rows of $M$ are the
all-red row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$; on $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$

$$r_{1}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a)t^{T},$$

i.e. $b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  The same two
column types occur, $c_{0}=a{\bf1}_{m}$ and
$c_{1}=a{\bf1}_{m}+(b-a)s$.  For a non-trivial canton
$s\not\propto{\bf1}_{m}$, $t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and for $a\ne b$
$r_{0},r_{1}$ are independent, e.g.

\[
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,\qquad
\det =b(a-b)\ne0,
\]

so that generically

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=1+1=2,\qquad a\ne b,
$$

inessential all-one factor the non-trivial red-white part is the
essentially rank-one matrix $W=s t^{T}$.

      +{\bf1}_{H_{r}}(i){\bf1}_{V_{c}}(j)\Bigr],
\end{equation*}

   =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=s\,t^{T},$$

$$s_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}(i),\qquad 
t_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}(j),$$
and $W\equiv0$ outside $R_{c}\times C_{c}$.  Hence, up to zero padding,

$${\rm White}=(R_{c}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c}),$$
the four corner rectangles of the canton, and

$${\rm rk}W=1,\qquad 
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)s_{i}t_{j}=aJ+(b-a)s t^{T}
\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},s\}\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},t\}.$$

$i\in H_{r}$ and $r_{1}$ the $R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ rows which are $b$
on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ elsewhere, with the symmetric two

$t\not\propto{\bf1}_{n}$ and for $a\ne b$

$$\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M,\qquad
