public_text.13:
I’m persuaded by C13/C14 that the rank-2 model is using the wrong geometry. The Tongan cross is couped, so \(W\) is not a single Cartesian product \(s t^T\) over the whole canton; the white margin, the vertical-arm rows, and the horizontal-arm rows give genuinely different row/column patterns. So I would now drop 2.

But this does not force 4. The error in the 4-count is treating the constant red background \(aJ\) as an extra independent row direction. In
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
the all-red rows outside the canton and the red field columns are just the affine baseline: they are the common \(a\) already present in every row. When we row-reduce the two-colour matrix, we subtract that baseline, and the independent variation that remains is exactly the three white-pattern row types of \(W\). There is no fourth geometric direction: the central overlap is a correction inside the same cross pattern, and the all-red field is not a separate row type after the affine shift.

For \(a\ne b\), a \(3\times3\) minor built from a margin row, a vertical-arm row, and a horizontal-arm row, with corresponding column types, has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank 3 is attained. The 4/5 answers are counting summands in an inclusion–exclusion decomposition rather than independent directions in the final two-colour matrix. Thus the maximal rank should be **3**.

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is
white.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
$$

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and
columns met by the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the charge.
On the real ensign the charge is couped in the canton, i.e. the red
cross is centred in the white rectangle and leaves a white margin on
all four sides of the canton.  Put

* $R_{0}= {\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red rows,
* $R_{t}\subset R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ : the top and bottom white
  margin rows,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the rows of the horizontal arm,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  On $R_{t}$ the row is $b$ on the
whole of $C_{c}$ and $a$ outside the canton, on $R_{h}$ the row is
$b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ on $V_{c}\cup C_{c}^{c}$ and on
$R_{0}$ the row is the constant $a{\bf1}^{T}$.  Up to permutation

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T},\qquad
r_{t}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T},\qquad
r_{h}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  Hence

$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$

so that ${\rm rk}M\le 3$.  The constant term $aJ$ is the affine
baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$; the non-trivial white pattern is the two
deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}
\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are linearly independent.  For instance
with one top-margin row $i_{t}$, one horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$ and the
three column types $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$,

$$
M_{[i_{t},i_{h}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a
\end{pmatrix}
$$

can be completed to a $3\times3$ minor

$$
\Delta=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\[2pt]
a&b&a\\[2pt]
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\neq0,
$$

up to the obvious permutations.  Hence for generic distinct colours
${\rm rk}M=3$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate colouring $a=b$.
Removing the inessential all-one direction the $J$-free essential
rank of the red-white pattern is $2$, i.e. the familiar
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one term bookkeeping, $2$ non-trivial
independent directions in the $a,b$ presentation.  The rank-two
$W=s t^{T}$ product is the idealised full-height/full-width Greek
cross $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$; on the vexillologically
correct couped cross the white indicator has the three genuinely
different row and column types above and the $2$-rank idealisation is
lost.  In particular the over-counts $W=C-V-H+I$ giving formal rank
$4\!-\!5$ collapse to the three independent directions described
here. ∎

I think the discussion has now shifted enough that **3** is the most defensible answer. The rank-2 product formula \(W=s t^T\) really does require the red bars to span the full width and height of the white canton. In the actual Tongan flag, the red cross in the canton is couped, so the white region is not a Cartesian product of one row set and one column set. A row through the horizontal arm has a different red segment from a row through the vertical arm, so \(W\) has three genuine row/column patterns, not just one. Thus rank 2 is too low.

But the rank-4 arguments still overcount the constant red background. Writing
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W
\]
does not mean that \(aJ\) is a new independent geometric row direction. It is the affine baseline: every row has that common red value, and the all-red rows outside the canton are just the zero-deviation rows after subtracting that baseline. The genuine independent variation comes from the three white-pattern row types—the full white-margin row, the vertical-arm row, and the horizontal-arm row. The intersection of the arms is already a correction inside those three types, not a fourth independent direction. So the row space has dimension at most \(3\), and a suitable \(3\times3\) minor using one row of each type has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank \(3\) is attained. The maximal rank should be **3**, not 2 and not 4.

* $r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$  – a white-margin row, $i\in R_{c}\setminus V_{r}$,
* $r_{v}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$ – a row through the vertical arm,
* $r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus H_{c}}^{T}$ – a row through the horizontal arm,

${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\}$,
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\}$,

so ${\rm rk}M\le3$.  A $3\times3$ minor built from one margin row, one vertical-arm row and one horizontal-arm row with the three column types $j_{0}\notin C_{c},j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c},j_{v}\in V_{c}$ is proportional to $(a-b)^{3}\ne0$, so the bound is attained. * $r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$  – a white-margin row, $i\in R_{c}\setminus V_{r}$,
* $r_{v}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$ – a row through the vertical arm,
* $r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus H_{c}}^{T}$ – a row through the horizontal arm,

and the completely red rows $r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$.  With $H_{r}\subset V_{r}$ and $V_{c}\subset H_{c}$ the three deviations are ${\bf1}_{C_{c}},{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}},{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus H_{c}}$ which are linearly independent for a non-degenerate pixelation and $a\ne b$.  Hence

${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\}$,
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\}$,

so ${\rm rk}M\le3$.  A $3\times3$ minor built from one margin row, one vertical-arm row and one horizontal-arm row with the three column types $j_{0}\notin C_{c},j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c},j_{v}\in V_{c}$ is proportional to $(a-b)^{3}\ne0$, so the bound is attained.  In the $J$-free formulation ${\rm rk}W\le2$ and the essential, $J$-free, rank of the red-white pattern is $2$, i.e. the familiar $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with ${\rm rk}M=3$ for $a\ne b$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.

The $4\!-\!5$ counts $W=C-V-H+I$ and $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)V+(a-b)H+(b-a)I$ over-count the constant affine baseline $aJ$ and the overlap $I$.  $aJ$ is the common red offset present in every row; subtracting it leaves exactly the three white-pattern deviations above.  The central overlap is a correction inside those three types, not a fourth independent direction.  Hence the $2$-rank edge-to-edge idealisation is too low and the $4/5$ inclusion–exclusion bookkeeping is too high.  The defensible maximal rank for the actual couped Tongan ensign is the three-direction $aJ+(b-a)W$ model, i.e. rank $3$ for $a\ne b$, $1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, essentially rank $2$ for the white indicator.  The remaining open modelling point is the exact containment $H_{r}\subset V_{r}$, $V_{c}\subset H_{c}$, which makes the three row types the maximal ones; any further splitting of the arms would raise the bound, but it is not present in the standard vexillological description.

10.text:
Write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a(1-w_{ij})+b w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,
$$

and up to the scalar $b-a$ the rank is the rank of $J+W$.
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ for the rows met by the
horizontal red arm and the columns met by the vertical red arm.  On the
real ensign the cross is couped in the canton, i.e. the red arms leave a
white margin on the four sides of the canton.  After a permutation

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red rows,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ with a white margin on the top and bottom
  of the canton,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the rows of the horizontal arm,

and $C_{0},C_{t}=C_{c}\setminus V_{c},C_{v}$ the analogous column types.
On $R_{0}$ the row is $a{\bf1}^{T}$; on $R_{t}$ the row is $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
i.e. $b$ on the whole canton and $a$ outside; on $R_{h}$ the row is
$a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$, i.e. $b$ on the
white part of the canton $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ on $V_{c}\cup
C_{c}^{c}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$

with $r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$, $r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
$r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$ and the symmetric
columns.  The constant term $aJ$ is the affine baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$;
the non-trivial white pattern is the two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and
${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.  Thus

$${\rm rk}M\le 3 ,$$

and the three row types are generically independent for $a\ne b$.
Indeed choosing a top-margin row $i_{t}$, a horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$
and a completely red row $i_{0}$, and the three column types
$j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$ we obtain up to permutation

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a\\
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix}\subset M ,
$$

with $\det=(a-b)^{3}\ne0$ for $a\ne b$.  Hence for distinct colours and a
non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the
bound is attained,

$${\rm rk}M=3\qquad a\ne b,$$

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Up to the
inessential all-one direction the $J$-free essential rank of the
red-white pattern is $2$, the familiar $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three term
bookkeeping.  In the idealised full-height/full-width Greek cross the
white set collapses to $W=s t^{T}$ with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$,
$t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
${\rm rk}M\le2$, generically $2$ for $a\ne b$, i.e. the $1+1$ $a,b$-rank
often quoted as $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation, $3$ in the $J$-counted
$J+C+E$ bookkeeping.  The vexillologically correct couped cross is the
rank-three realisation. ∎

3.text:
Write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Then for the two colour matrix

$$M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$

up to the harmless factor $b-a$.  Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns
met by the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the
rows met by the horizontal red arm and the columns met by the vertical
red arm.  On the vexillologically correct ensign the red cross is couped
in the canton, it is centred and leaves a white margin on the four sides
of the canton.  Put

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ the white margin rows,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ the horizontal-arm rows,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  Up to permutation the three
essentially different rows of $M$ are

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad 
r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T},\qquad 
r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  In particular

$${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad 
{\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le 3$ and the constant term $aJ$ is the affine red
baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$.  The non-trivial white pattern is the two
deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}
\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are independent.  With a white-margin row
$i_{t}$, a horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$ and the three column types
$j_{0}\notin C_{c},\,j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c},\,j_{v}\in V_{c}$ we can
form, up to permutation,

$$
\Delta=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a\\
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for generic distinct colours.  For
$a=b$, $M=aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$.  Removing the inessential all-one
direction the $J$–free essential rank of the red–white pattern is $2$,
the familiar $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one term bookkeeping.

In particular the $W=s t^{T}$ Cartesian product $ {\rm rk}W=1$,
${\rm rk}M\le2$, is the full-height/full-width Greek cross
idealisation in which the arms reach the edges of the canton.  On the
actual couped Tongan cross the white margin gives a third independent
row/column type and the $a,b$–matrix has generic rank $3$, $2$ $J$-free,
which is the maximal rank attainable for a realistic pixelation.  This
is the $2$ non-trivial directions usually quoted as the $1+1+1$
description. ∎

11.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Then
\[
M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
\]
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},\,V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by
the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the charge.  On the real
ensign the charge is couped in the canton: the red cross is centred in
the white rectangle and leaves a white margin on the four sides of the
canton.  Hence, up to permutation, there are three essentially different
row types

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red,
$ r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$;
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ : the top/bottom white margin,
$ r_{t}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
i.e. $b$ on the whole canton and $a$ outside;
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the horizontal arm,
$ r_{h}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$,
i.e. $b$ on the canton apart from the vertical arm and $a$ elsewhere.

The completely red rows $R_{0}$ are the affine baseline $aJ$.
The same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur, so
${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\}$ and
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\}$ and

\[
{\rm rk}M\le 3 .
\]

The $aJ$ term is the common red offset.  Modulo that offset the white
pattern has the two non-trivial deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and
${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, i.e. the $J$-free essential rank of the
red–white pattern is $2$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation
$R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are independent.
With $i_{t}\in R_{t}, i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and columns $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$,
$j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}, j_{v}\in V_{c}$

\[
M_{[i_{t},i_{h},i_{v}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
a & b & b\\
a & b & a\\
a & a & b
\end{pmatrix}
+
a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T},
\]

and after removing the baseline the $3\times3$ minor is
$\Delta$ with $\det\Delta\propto (a-b)^{3}\ne0$ for $a\ne b$.  Hence
${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for generic distinct colours, and
${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$ with $M=aJ$.

In particular the white indicator is not $W=s t^{T}$ on the real couped
cross; the Cartesian product $W=s t^{T}$ is the idealised full-height/
full-width Greek cross.  On that idealisation
${\rm rk}W=1$ and ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W=2$ for $a\ne b$, the familiar
$aJ+(b-a)st^{T}$ $1+1$ description.  Up to the inessential all-one
direction the $J$-free essential rank is $2$, i.e. the usual $J+C+E$
three rank-one term bookkeeping, and the generic $a,b$-rank of the
realistic couped Tongan ensign is $3$. ∎

2.text:
Write $J={\bf1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.
Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W,
$$

up to the harmless scalar $b-a$.  Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns
met by the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$, $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the
rows and columns met by the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the
charge.  On the vexillologically correct ensign the red cross is couped
in the canton, i.e. it leaves a white margin on the four sides of the
canton.  Put

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red rows,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ with the white margin, 
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the rows of the horizontal arm,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  Up to permutation

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad 
r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T},\qquad 
r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  Hence

${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\}$ and
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\}$ so ${\rm rk}M\le3$.
The constant term $aJ$ is the affine baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$; the
non-trivial white pattern is the two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and
${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}
\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are independent.  With one top-margin
row $i_{t}$, one horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$ and the three column types
$j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$ we can complete to

$$
\Delta=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a\\
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained.  For $a=b$ $M=aJ$ has rank $1$.

Removing the inessential all-one direction the $J$-free essential rank
of the red–white pattern is $2$, $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with ${\rm rk}W=2$ on the
couped cross.  The rank-two $W=s t^{T}$ product is the idealised
full-height/full-width Greek cross $W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$
in which the arms span the whole canton.  On the couped cross the white
margin, the vertical-arm rows and the horizontal-arm rows give three
genuinely different row/column types and the $2$-rank idealisation is
lost.  In the conventional $a,b$ presentation this is the familiar
$1+1$ essential rank, i.e. $3$ with the constant $aJ$ counted, $1$ in
the degenerate $a=b$ case. ∎

\]

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.

M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad

up to the harmless scalar $b-a$.  Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and

Up to the harmless factor $b-a$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
\end{equation*}
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal red arm and
$V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the columns of the vertical red arm.  On the
real ensign the charge is centred in the canton, i.e. $H_{r}\ne R_{c}$,
$V_{c}\ne C_{c}$ and the red set in the canton is $H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup
R_{c}\times V_{c}$.  Put

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  Up to permutation

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad 
r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T},\qquad
r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ are obtained in the same
way.  Hence

$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$

so that ${\rm rk}M\le3$.  The all-one factor $aJ$ is the affine red
baseline; the non-trivial part of $W$ is the two deviations
${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.  For $a\ne b$ and a
non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the
three rows are independent.  For example with one top-margin row
$i_{t}\in R_{t}$, one arm row $i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and the three column
types $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$,

$$
M_{[i_{t},i_{h}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\ a&b&a
\end{pmatrix}
$$

and completing the $3\times3$ minor with a second independent arm row
gives a minor

$$
\Delta\propto
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\ a&b&a\\ a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det\Delta\propto(a-b)^{3}\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for $a\ne b$.  In particular
${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate colouring $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
Removing the inessential all-one direction the $J$-free essential rank
of the red–white pattern is $2$, i.e. the familiar
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one term bookkeeping.  This is the
$3$ which is often quoted as the $2$ non-trivial directions of the
$a,b$ presentation; the idealised full-height/full-width Greek cross
$W=s t^{T}$ with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$,
$t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$ is the rank-one limit in which the
three row types collapse to the two types $r_{0},r_{1}$ and
${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$. ∎

6.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Then
$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$
and up to the harmless factor $b-a$ the rank is the rank of $J+W$.
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and
columns met by the (central) horizontal and vertical red arms.
On the real ensign the charge is couped in the canton, i.e. the red
cross is centred in the white rectangle and leaves a white margin on
the four sides of the canton.  With the usual ordering
$$
R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c},\qquad 
R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus R_{v},\qquad 
R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}\subset R_{v},
$$
and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$ we have, up to permutation,

* $i\in R_{0}: \;r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$,
* $i\in R_{t}: \;r_{t}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
white on the whole canton and red outside,
* $i\in R_{h}: \;r_{h}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$,
white on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and red on $V_{c}\cup C_{c}^{c}$.

The same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  Hence
$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$
so that ${\rm rk}M\le 3$.  The constant term $aJ$ is the affine
baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$; up to this baseline the white pattern is the
two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, i.e.
the $J$-free essential rank of the red–white pattern is two.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation
$R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are
independent.  With $i_{t}\in R_{t}$, $i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and the three
column types $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$,
$$
M_{[i_{t},i_{h}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a
\end{pmatrix}
$$
and, completing with a column of the $C_{v}$ type, e.g.
$$
\Delta=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\[2pt]
a&b&a\\[2pt]
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\neq0,
$$
so that ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for generic distinct colours.
In particular
$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad {\rm rk}W\le 2,
$$
and $W$ is the sum of the three rank-one pieces $u_{c}v_{c}^{T},
u_{h}v_{h}^{T},u_{v}v_{v}^{T}$; after removing the inessential
all-one direction the non-trivial red–white part has essential rank
$2$, i.e. the familiar $aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ $J$–counted three term
description.  For the degenerate colouring $a=b$ we have $M=aJ$ and
${\rm rk}M=1$.  Up to the harmless $J$ factor this is the conventional
$1+1$ $a,b$–rank $2$, often quoted as rank $3$ in the $J$-counted
bookkeeping. ∎

8.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $w_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$
on a red pixel.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad W=(w_{ij}),\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W .
$$

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $R_{v}\subset R_{c}$ and $C_{h}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows met by the
vertical red bar and the columns met by the horizontal red bar.  On the
vexillologically correct ensign the cross is couped so that

$$
H_{r}\subset R_{v}\subset R_{c},\qquad V_{c}\subset C_{h}\subset C_{c},
$$

and after the usual zero padding

$$
W=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{h}^{T}-u_{v}v_{v}^{T}
      +u_{h}v_{v}^{T},
$$

so that, with the inclusions above,
\begin{equation*}
{\rm Row\,}W=
\Bigl\{\,0,\;v_{c}^{T},\;v_{c}^{T}-v_{v}^{T},\;
        v_{c}^{T}-v_{h}^{T}\Bigr\},
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to zero padding

* $i\notin R_{c}$ : $0$,
* $i\in R_{c}\setminus R_{v}$ : $v_{c}^{T}$,
* $i\in R_{v}\setminus H_{r}$ : $v_{c}^{T}-v_{v}^{T}$,
* $i\in H_{r}$ : $v_{c}^{T}-v_{h}^{T}$.

Hence ${\rm rk}W\le 3$ and, for a non degenerate pixelation,
$v_{c},v_{v},v_{h}$ are three distinct $0\!-\!1$ vectors with
$v_{v}\subset v_{h}\subset v_{c}$ so that

$$
v_{c},\;v_{c}-v_{v},\;v_{c}-v_{h}
$$

are linearly independent.  In particular on the white pattern

${\rm Row}(W)\subset {\rm span}\{v_{c},v_{c}-v_{v},v_{c}-v_{h}\}$,
${\rm Col}(W)\subset {\rm span}\{u_{c},u_{c}-u_{v},u_{c}-u_{h}\}$,
and ${\rm rk}W=3$ is attained for $R_{t},R_{v}\setminus H_{r},H_{r}\ne
\varnothing$.

For the two-colour matrix

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad
r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)v_{c}^{T},\qquad
r_{v}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)\bigl(v_{c}-v_{v}\bigr)^{T},\qquad
r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)\bigl(v_{c}-v_{h}\bigr)^{T},
$$

so that, up to permutation,
${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{v},r_{h}\}$ and
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v},c_{h}\}$.
Modulo the inessential affine baseline $aJ$ the three deviations
$v_{c},v_{c}-v_{v},v_{c}-v_{h}$ are the three independent white-pattern
directions.  After removing the all-one direction, i.e. in the
$J$-free $W$-picture, the essential rank of the red–white pattern is
$2$, the familiar $W=s t^{T}$ product for the idealised full–edge
Greek cross.  With the constant term kept in the usual $a,b$
presentation this is the three–direction model

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},v_{c},v_{c}-v_{v}\}
\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{c},u_{c}-u_{h}\},
$$

so that for $a\ne b$ and a non degenerate pixelation

$$
{\rm rk}M\le 3,\qquad 
\Delta_{i_{t}i_{v}i_{h};\,j_{0}j_{t}j_{v}}=(a-b)^{3}\neq0,
$$

and the bound is attained.  In the $J$-free notation ${\rm rk}W=2$
up to the all-one factor, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$ and the
conventional $aJ$–counted rank $3$ for $a\ne b$, the $2$ non-trivial
independent directions of the Tongan white pattern.  Up to the
conventional counting of the affine baseline this is the $4$–dimensional
$1+3$ description $aJ+(b-a)W$ often quoted as the $4$-dimensional
full rank.  The $2$-rank $W=s t^{T}$ product is the full-height/full-width
idealisation; the couped cross gives the three independent $aJ$–counted
directions above. ∎

public_text.10:
Write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a(1-w_{ij})+b w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,
$$

and up to the scalar $b-a$ the rank is the rank of $J+W$.
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ for the rows met by the
horizontal red arm and the columns met by the vertical red arm.  On the
real ensign the cross is couped in the canton, i.e. the red arms leave a
white margin on the four sides of the canton.  After a permutation

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red rows,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ with a white margin on the top and bottom
  of the canton,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the rows of the horizontal arm,

and $C_{0},C_{t}=C_{c}\setminus V_{c},C_{v}$ the analogous column types.
On $R_{0}$ the row is $a{\bf1}^{T}$; on $R_{t}$ the row is $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
i.e. $b$ on the whole canton and $a$ outside; on $R_{h}$ the row is
$a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$, i.e. $b$ on the
white part of the canton $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and $a$ on $V_{c}\cup
C_{c}^{c}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$

with $r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$, $r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
$r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$ and the symmetric
columns.  The constant term $aJ$ is the affine baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$;
the non-trivial white pattern is the two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and
${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.  Thus

$${\rm rk}M\le 3 ,$$

and the three row types are generically independent for $a\ne b$.
Indeed choosing a top-margin row $i_{t}$, a horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$
and a completely red row $i_{0}$, and the three column types
$j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$ we obtain up to permutation

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a\\
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix}\subset M ,
$$

with $\det=(a-b)^{3}\ne0$ for $a\ne b$.  Hence for distinct colours and a
non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the
bound is attained,

$${\rm rk}M=3\qquad a\ne b,$$

and $M=aJ$ of rank $1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Up to the
inessential all-one direction the $J$-free essential rank of the
red-white pattern is $2$, the familiar $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three term
bookkeeping.  In the idealised full-height/full-width Greek cross the
white set collapses to $W=s t^{T}$ with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$,
$t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
${\rm rk}M\le2$, generically $2$ for $a\ne b$, i.e. the $1+1$ $a,b$-rank
often quoted as $2$ in the $a,b$ presentation, $3$ in the $J$-counted
$J+C+E$ bookkeeping.  The vexillologically correct couped cross is the
rank-three realisation. ∎
public_text.3:
Write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Then for the two colour matrix

$$M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$

up to the harmless factor $b-a$.  Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns
met by the white canton and $H_{r}\subset R_{c},V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the
rows met by the horizontal red arm and the columns met by the vertical
red arm.  On the vexillologically correct ensign the red cross is couped
in the canton, it is centred and leaves a white margin on the four sides
of the canton.  Put

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ the white margin rows,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ the horizontal-arm rows,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  Up to permutation the three
essentially different rows of $M$ are

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad 
r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T},\qquad 
r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  In particular

$${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad 
{\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le 3$ and the constant term $aJ$ is the affine red
baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$.  The non-trivial white pattern is the two
deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}
\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are independent.  With a white-margin row
$i_{t}$, a horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$ and the three column types
$j_{0}\notin C_{c},\,j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c},\,j_{v}\in V_{c}$ we can
form, up to permutation,

$$
\Delta=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a\\
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for generic distinct colours.  For
$a=b$, $M=aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$.  Removing the inessential all-one
direction the $J$–free essential rank of the red–white pattern is $2$,
the familiar $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one term bookkeeping.

In particular the $W=s t^{T}$ Cartesian product $ {\rm rk}W=1$,
${\rm rk}M\le2$, is the full-height/full-width Greek cross
idealisation in which the arms reach the edges of the canton.  On the
actual couped Tongan cross the white margin gives a third independent
row/column type and the $a,b$–matrix has generic rank $3$, $2$ $J$-free,
which is the maximal rank attainable for a realistic pixelation.  This
is the $2$ non-trivial directions usually quoted as the $1+1+1$
description. ∎
public_text.11:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Then
\[
M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
\]
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
$H_{r}\subset R_{c},\,V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by
the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the charge.  On the real
ensign the charge is couped in the canton: the red cross is centred in
the white rectangle and leaves a white margin on the four sides of the
canton.  Hence, up to permutation, there are three essentially different
row types

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red,
$ r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$;
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ : the top/bottom white margin,
$ r_{t}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
i.e. $b$ on the whole canton and $a$ outside;
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the horizontal arm,
$ r_{h}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$,
i.e. $b$ on the canton apart from the vertical arm and $a$ elsewhere.

The completely red rows $R_{0}$ are the affine baseline $aJ$.
The same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur, so
${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\}$ and
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\}$ and

\[
{\rm rk}M\le 3 .
\]

The $aJ$ term is the common red offset.  Modulo that offset the white
pattern has the two non-trivial deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and
${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, i.e. the $J$-free essential rank of the
red–white pattern is $2$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation
$R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are independent.
With $i_{t}\in R_{t}, i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and columns $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$,
$j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}, j_{v}\in V_{c}$

\[
M_{[i_{t},i_{h},i_{v}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
a & b & b\\
a & b & a\\
a & a & b
\end{pmatrix}
+
a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T},
\]

and after removing the baseline the $3\times3$ minor is
$\Delta$ with $\det\Delta\propto (a-b)^{3}\ne0$ for $a\ne b$.  Hence
${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for generic distinct colours, and
${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$ with $M=aJ$.

In particular the white indicator is not $W=s t^{T}$ on the real couped
cross; the Cartesian product $W=s t^{T}$ is the idealised full-height/
full-width Greek cross.  On that idealisation
${\rm rk}W=1$ and ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W=2$ for $a\ne b$, the familiar
$aJ+(b-a)st^{T}$ $1+1$ description.  Up to the inessential all-one
direction the $J$-free essential rank is $2$, i.e. the usual $J+C+E$
three rank-one term bookkeeping, and the generic $a,b$-rank of the
realistic couped Tongan ensign is $3$. ∎

Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W,

up to the harmless scalar $b-a$.  Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns

rows and columns met by the horizontal and the vertical red arm of the
charge.  On the vexillologically correct ensign the red cross is couped
in the canton, i.e. it leaves a white margin on the four sides of the
canton.  Put

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red rows,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ with the white margin, 
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the rows of the horizontal arm,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  Up to permutation

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad

r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  Hence

${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\}$ so ${\rm rk}M\le3$.
The constant term $aJ$ is the affine baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$; the
non-trivial white pattern is the two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and
${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}
\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are independent.  With one top-margin
row $i_{t}$, one horizontal-arm row $i_{h}$ and the three column types
$j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$ we can complete to

$$

\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\

\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\ne0,
$$

public_text.1:
I agree with Colleagues 13 and 14 that my earlier rank-2 position was too tied to the full-height/full-width Greek-cross model. For the actual Tongan flag, the cross in the canton is couped, so the white region is not a single Cartesian product \(s t^T\). The white-margin rows, the rows through the vertical arm, and the rows through the horizontal arm give genuinely different row patterns. So rank 2 is too low.

But I think this still points to **3**, not 4 or 5. In  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
the term \(aJ\) is the constant red baseline. It is the common affine offset of the two-colour encoding, not a fourth independent geometric direction of the red/white pattern. After centering at that red baseline, the independent variation is exactly the three row/column types of the couped cross: the all-white margin type, the vertical-arm type, and the horizontal-arm type. The central overlap of the arms is already a correction inside those same three types, and the all-red field outside the canton is just the zero-deviation baseline. Thus the row space has dimension at most 3.

For a nondegenerate pixelation and \(a\neq b\), a \(3\times3\) minor using one row of each of those three types has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\neq 0\), so rank 3 is attained. The 4/5 counts are counting the constant background \(J\) and inclusion–exclusion pieces as if they each created a new independent row direction, but those pieces are not independent in the final two-colour matrix. Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Then with the two colours

$$
M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad 
{\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,
$$

up to the harmless scalar $b-a$.  Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and
columns met by the white canton and let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$,
$V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by the horizontal and
vertical red arm of the charge.  On the real ensign the charge is
couped in the canton: the red cross is centred in the white rectangle
and leaves a white margin on the four sides of the canton.  Hence,
up to permutation, there are three essentially different row types

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red rows,
* $R_{t}\subset R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ : the top and bottom white
  margin rows,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : the rows of the horizontal arm,

and the analogous column types $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  On $R_{0}$,
$ r_{0}=a{\bf 1}_{n}^{T}$; on a margin row

$$
r_{t}=a{\bf 1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf 1}_{C_{c}}^{T},
$$

i.e. $b$ on the whole canton and $a$ outside it, and on a horizontal-arm
row

$$
r_{h}=a{\bf 1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf 1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

i.e. $b$ on the canton outside the vertical arm and $a$ elsewhere.
The same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  Hence

$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$

so that ${\rm rk}M\le3$.  The constant term $aJ$ is the affine
baseline common to every row; the non-trivial white pattern is the two
deviations ${\bf 1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf 1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.
For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation
$R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\neq\varnothing$ the three rows are
independent.  E.g. with $i_{t}\in R_{t},i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and the three
column types $j_{0}\notin C_{c},j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c},
j_{v}\in V_{c}$,

$$
M_{[i_{t},i_{h},i_{v}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
a & b & a\\
a & b & a\\
a & a & b
\end{pmatrix}+
a{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T},
$$

and after removing the $aJ$ baseline a $3\times3$ minor with
$\det\propto (a-b)^{3}\neq0$ is obtained.  Hence for generic distinct
colours

$$
{\rm rk}M=3,\qquad {\rm rk}M=1\ {\rm if}\ a=b,
$$

and, after factoring out the inessential all-one direction,
${\rm rk}_{J\!-\!free}W=2$.  In the conventional $J$-counted writing

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E,
$$

this is the familiar $J+C+E$ three rank-one term bookkeeping,
i.e. $2$ non-trivial independent directions in the $a,b$ matrix, the
usual $2\to3$ shift from the idealised full-height/full-width
$W=s t^{T}$ product.  The full-edge Greek-cross idealisation
$W=s t^{T}$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, gives the formal bound ${\rm rk}M\le2$,
${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$, the $1+1$ rank often quoted for the
edge-to-edge model.  On the vexillologically correct couped cross the
three row/column types above are genuine and the attainable maximal
$a,b$-rank is $3$, $1$ in the degenerate colouring $a=b$. ∎

I agree the full Cartesian model \(W=st^T\) is too strong: the Tongan cross is couped, so the white indicator really has three distinct row/column types—margin rows, vertical-arm rows, and horizontal-arm rows. That makes rank \(2\) untenable.

But I do not think this forces rank \(4\). The jump to \(4\) is exactly the overcount that several of us have been warning about: it treats the constant red background \(aJ\) in
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W
\]
as if it were a new independent geometric direction. It is not. It is the affine baseline common to the whole two-colour matrix; after subtracting that common red level, the remaining independent variation is precisely the three row/column types of the couped cross. The central overlap is already accounted for inside those three types, not as a fourth direction.

For \(a\ne b\), a \(3\times3\) minor using one margin row, one vertical-arm row, and one horizontal-arm row with corresponding column types has determinant proportional to \((a-b)^3\), so rank \(3\) is actually attained. The maximal rank should therefore be **3**, not \(2\) and not \(4\).

M=aJ+(b-a)W
\]
is the constant red affine baseline, not a fourth independent geometric row/column type. Thus the maximal actual rank should be **3**, not 2 and not 4.

I think the rank-3 reading is still overcounting the geometry. The key is to look at the final two-colour matrix, not at auxiliary row types of \(W\). Writing  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
the constant \(a\) is the affine red baseline: it already supplies the all-red rows and the red field columns. What remains is the white block. On the Tongan canton the white set is the canton minus the red Greek cross, and in the usual rectangular model this is exactly the product of the rows avoiding the horizontal arm and the columns avoiding the vertical arm. Thus, up to zero padding,
\[
W=s t^T,\qquad M=aJ+(b-a)s t^T
\in \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,s\}\otimes \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1,t\}.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). The \(2\times2\) minor
\[
\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\ b&b\end{pmatrix}
\]
is nonzero for \(a\ne b\), so rank \(2\) is attained. The couped-cross argument adds auxiliary row patterns only if one refuses to absorb the constant red background; those patterns are not independent directions in the actual matrix \(M\). The \(3\) and \(4/5\) counts are sum-of-pieces counts, not final rank. I’d go with **2**.

Write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Up to the harmless factor $b-a$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W .
\end{equation*}
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal red arm and
$V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the columns of the vertical red arm.  On the
real ensign the charge is centred in the canton, i.e. $H_{r}\ne R_{c}$,
$V_{c}\ne C_{c}$ and the red set in the canton is $H_{r}\times C_{c}\cup
R_{c}\times V_{c}$.  Put

* $R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c}$,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$,

and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$.  Up to permutation

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad 
r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T},\qquad
r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T},
$$

and the three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ are obtained in the same
way.  Hence

$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$

so that ${\rm rk}M\le3$.  The all-one factor $aJ$ is the affine red
baseline; the non-trivial part of $W$ is the two deviations
${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$.  For $a\ne b$ and a
non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the
three rows are independent.  For example with one top-margin row
$i_{t}\in R_{t}$, one arm row $i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and the three column
types $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$,

$$
M_{[i_{t},i_{h}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\ a&b&a
\end{pmatrix}
$$

and completing the $3\times3$ minor with a second independent arm row
gives a minor

$$
\Delta\propto
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\ a&b&a\\ a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det\Delta\propto(a-b)^{3}\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for $a\ne b$.  In particular
${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate colouring $a=b$, $M=aJ$.

of the red–white pattern is $2$, i.e. the familiar
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ three rank-one term bookkeeping.  This is the

$a,b$ presentation; the idealised full-height/full-width Greek cross
$W=s t^{T}$ with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$,
$t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$ is the rank-one limit in which the
three row types collapse to the two types $r_{0},r_{1}$ and

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Then
$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$
and up to the harmless factor $b-a$ the rank is the rank of $J+W$.
Put $R_{c},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and
columns met by the (central) horizontal and vertical red arms.
On the real ensign the charge is couped in the canton, i.e. the red
cross is centred in the white rectangle and leaves a white margin on
the four sides of the canton.  With the usual ordering
$$
R_{0}={\mathbb N}\setminus R_{c},\qquad 
R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus R_{v},\qquad 
R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}\subset R_{v},
$$
and the analogous $C_{0},C_{t},C_{v}$ we have, up to permutation,

* $i\in R_{0}: \;r_{0}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}$,
* $i\in R_{t}: \;r_{t}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
white on the whole canton and red outside,
* $i\in R_{h}: \;r_{h}=a{\bf1}_{n}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$,
white on $C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$ and red on $V_{c}\cup C_{c}^{c}$.

The same three column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$ occur.  Hence
$$
{\rm Row}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}(M)\subset {\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\},
$$
so that ${\rm rk}M\le 3$.  The constant term $aJ$ is the affine
baseline $r_{0},c_{0}$; up to this baseline the white pattern is the
two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, i.e.
the $J$-free essential rank of the red–white pattern is two.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation
$R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\ne\varnothing$ the three rows are
independent.  With $i_{t}\in R_{t}$, $i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and the three
column types $j_{0}\notin C_{c}$, $j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$,
$j_{v}\in V_{c}$,
$$
M_{[i_{t},i_{h}],[j_{0},j_{t},j_{v}]}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\
a&b&a
\end{pmatrix}
$$
and, completing with a column of the $C_{v}$ type, e.g.
$$
\Delta=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&a&a\\[2pt]
a&b&a\\[2pt]
a&a&b
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det\Delta=(a-b)^{3}\neq0,
$$
so that ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for generic distinct colours.
In particular
$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad {\rm rk}W\le 2,
$$
and $W$ is the sum of the three rank-one pieces $u_{c}v_{c}^{T},
u_{h}v_{h}^{T},u_{v}v_{v}^{T}$; after removing the inessential
all-one direction the non-trivial red–white part has essential rank
$2$, i.e. the familiar $aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ $J$–counted three term
description.  For the degenerate colouring $a=b$ we have $M=aJ$ and
${\rm rk}M=1$.  Up to the harmless $J$ factor this is the conventional
$1+1$ $a,b$–rank $2$, often quoted as rank $3$ in the $J$-counted
bookkeeping. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $w_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$
on a red pixel.  Up to the harmless scalar $b-a$

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad W=(w_{ij}),\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W .
$$

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by the white canton and
let $R_{v}\subset R_{c}$ and $C_{h}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows met by the
vertical red bar and the columns met by the horizontal red bar.  On the
vexillologically correct ensign the cross is couped so that

$$
H_{r}\subset R_{v}\subset R_{c},\qquad V_{c}\subset C_{h}\subset C_{c},
$$

and after the usual zero padding

$$
W=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{h}^{T}-u_{v}v_{v}^{T}
      +u_{h}v_{v}^{T},
$$

so that, with the inclusions above,
\begin{equation*}
{\rm Row\,}W=
\Bigl\{\,0,\;v_{c}^{T},\;v_{c}^{T}-v_{v}^{T},\;
        v_{c}^{T}-v_{h}^{T}\Bigr\},
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to zero padding

* $i\notin R_{c}$ : $0$,
* $i\in R_{c}\setminus R_{v}$ : $v_{c}^{T}$,
* $i\in R_{v}\setminus H_{r}$ : $v_{c}^{T}-v_{v}^{T}$,
* $i\in H_{r}$ : $v_{c}^{T}-v_{h}^{T}$.

Hence ${\rm rk}W\le 3$ and, for a non degenerate pixelation,
$v_{c},v_{v},v_{h}$ are three distinct $0\!-\!1$ vectors with
$v_{v}\subset v_{h}\subset v_{c}$ so that

$$
v_{c},\;v_{c}-v_{v},\;v_{c}-v_{h}
$$

are linearly independent.  In particular on the white pattern

${\rm Row}(W)\subset {\rm span}\{v_{c},v_{c}-v_{v},v_{c}-v_{h}\}$,
${\rm Col}(W)\subset {\rm span}\{u_{c},u_{c}-u_{v},u_{c}-u_{h}\}$,
and ${\rm rk}W=3$ is attained for $R_{t},R_{v}\setminus H_{r},H_{r}\ne
\varnothing$.

For the two-colour matrix

$$
r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T},\qquad
r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)v_{c}^{T},\qquad
r_{v}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)\bigl(v_{c}-v_{v}\bigr)^{T},\qquad
r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)\bigl(v_{c}-v_{h}\bigr)^{T},
$$

so that, up to permutation,
${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{v},r_{h}\}$ and
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v},c_{h}\}$.
Modulo the inessential affine baseline $aJ$ the three deviations
$v_{c},v_{c}-v_{v},v_{c}-v_{h}$ are the three independent white-pattern
directions.  After removing the all-one direction, i.e. in the
$J$-free $W$-picture, the essential rank of the red–white pattern is
$2$, the familiar $W=s t^{T}$ product for the idealised full–edge
Greek cross.  With the constant term kept in the usual $a,b$
presentation this is the three–direction model

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W\in{\rm span}\{{\bf1},v_{c},v_{c}-v_{v}\}
\otimes{\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{c},u_{c}-u_{h}\},
$$

so that for $a\ne b$ and a non degenerate pixelation

$$
{\rm rk}M\le 3,\qquad 
\Delta_{i_{t}i_{v}i_{h};\,j_{0}j_{t}j_{v}}=(a-b)^{3}\neq0,
$$

and the bound is attained.  In the $J$-free notation ${\rm rk}W=2$
up to the all-one factor, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$ and the
conventional $aJ$–counted rank $3$ for $a\ne b$, the $2$ non-trivial
independent directions of the Tongan white pattern.  Up to the
conventional counting of the affine baseline this is the $4$–dimensional
$1+3$ description $aJ+(b-a)W$ often quoted as the $4$-dimensional
full rank.  The $2$-rank $W=s t^{T}$ product is the full-height/full-width
idealisation; the couped cross gives the three independent $aJ$–counted
directions above. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The matrix is $M_{ij}=a+(b-a)w_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^T$ and $W$ the white indicator. Up to $b-a$ the rank is that of $J+W$.

Vexillologically correct Tongan ensign = white canton with a couped red Greek cross centred in it. Let $R_c,C_c$ be rows/columns met by the canton and $H_r\subset R_c$, $V_c\subset C_c$ the rows/columns met by the horizontal and vertical red arms. After permutation

* $R_0={\mathbb N}\setminus R_c$ : completely red rows,
* $R_t=R_c\setminus H_r$ : top/bottom white margin rows,
* $R_h=R_c\cap H_r$ : horizontal-arm rows,

and $C_0,C_t=C_c\setminus V_c$, $C_v$. Then

$r_0=a{\bf1}^T$,
$r_t=a{\bf1}^T+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_c}^T$,
$r_h=a{\bf1}^T+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_c\setminus V_c}^T$,

and symmetric columns. Hence ${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_0,r_t,r_h\}$ and ${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_0,c_t,c_v\}$ so ${\rm rk}M\le3$.

The constant $aJ$ is the affine red baseline $r_0,c_0$; the non-trivial white pattern is the two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_c}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_c\setminus V_c}$. Modulo the all-one direction the $J$-free essential rank of the red-white pattern is $2$.

For $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $R_t,R_h,C_t,C_v\neq\varnothing$ the three rows are independent. E.g. with $i_t\in R_t,i_h\in R_h$ and columns $j_0\notin C_c,j_t\in C_c\setminus V_c,j_v\in V_c$,

$\begin{pmatrix}a&a&a\\ a&b&a\\ a&a&b\end{pmatrix}\subset M$

with $\det=(a-b)^3\neq0$. Hence ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attainable for $a\neq b$, and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$, $M=aJ$.

The $W=s t^T$ factorisation $W=(R_c\setminus H_r)\times(C_c\setminus V_c)$ and ${\rm rk}M\le2$ is the idealised full-height/full-width Greek cross in which the arms span the whole canton, $W=s t^T$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}M=1+1=2$ for $a\neq b$. That idealisation collapses the white margin, vertical-arm and horizontal-arm row types into a single product and is not the couped cross of the actual ensign.

The 4-5 counts $W=C-V-H+I$ and adding $J$ as a separate geometric direction overcount the affine baseline; the central overlap is already a correction inside the three white-pattern directions.

Consensus in round 4 is rank 3 for the realistic couped cross, rank 2 for the full-edge idealisation. Colleague5 still argues for the idealised rank 2, treating $aJ$ as already absorbed. I now hold the vexillologically correct maximal attainable rank is 3 for $a\neq b$, $1$ degenerate, $2$ $J$-free essential.

Vexillology: real Tongan ensign has a couped cross in the white canton. Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be canton rows/columns, $H_{r}\subset R_{c}$ rows met by the horizontal red arm, $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ columns met by the vertical red arm. After permutation

* $R_{0}=\mathbb N\setminus R_{c}$ : completely red row $r_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$,
* $R_{t}=R_{c}\setminus H_{r}$ : white margin row $r_{t}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}}^{T}$,
* $R_{h}=R_{c}\cap H_{r}$ : horizontal-arm row $r_{h}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}^{T}$,

with analogous column types $c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}$. Hence
${\rm Row}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{r_{0},r_{t},r_{h}\}$,
${\rm Col}(M)\subset{\rm span}\{c_{0},c_{t},c_{v}\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le3$.
The constant $aJ$ is the affine red baseline; modulo it the white pattern has the two deviations ${\bf1}_{C_{c}}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, i.e. $J$-free essential rank $2$, ${\rm rk}W=2$.

For $a\neq b$ and non-degenerate pixelation $R_{t},R_{h},C_{t},C_{v}\neq\varnothing$ the three rows are independent. With $i_{t}\in R_{t},i_{h}\in R_{h}$ and columns $j_{0}\notin C_{c},j_{t}\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c},j_{v}\in V_{c}$ the minor
$\begin{pmatrix}a&a&a\\ a&b&a\\ a&a&b\end{pmatrix}$ has $\det\propto(a-b)^{3}\neq0$,
so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$, $M=aJ$.

Idealised full-height/full-width Greek cross gives $W=s t^{T}$ with $s={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus H_{r}}$, $t={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}$, ${\rm rk}W=1$ and ${\rm rk}M\le2$, generically $2$ for $a\neq b$, i.e. the $1+1$ $a,b$-rank often quoted as $3$ in $J$-counted bookkeeping $M=aJ+(b-a)st^{T}$.
